title: Hrishikesh Mukherjee's 'Anand' lives on

title: Blast from the past: Parwana (1971)
claims: Kumar Sen's characterisation, the train-and-plane alibi, Bachchan shining in a negative role, the film's poor commercial result and Bachchan's comment on it.

title: Sunil Dutt sold 7 cars to make Reshma Aur Shera. It's an Indian Romeo & Juliet story
claims: Box-office flop; Chhotu's shooting of Chaudhury and Gopal; Chhotu hesitating to kill; Bachchan's performance conveying guilt, confusion and religious dread; casting as a mute because Dutt disliked his voice.

title: Classics Revisited: Guddi
claims: Stars including Amitabh Bachchan make special appearances shown at work in the studios; Bachchan was originally to play Jaya Bhaduri's hero.

title: Sanjog (1972)
claims: Mohan abandons Asha and remarries Seema; Asha becomes Collector with Mohan as her clerk; contrived climax; little scope for Bachchan; the music failed to lift the box office.

title: Revisiting Prakash Mehra's Zanjeer: The film that made Amitabh Bachchan
claims: Sleeper hit; Vijay as a brutally honest cop who treats every criminal as a personal enemy; created the Angry Young Man; Bachchan had 12 flops before it.

title: Birthday Special: 5 Amitabh Bachchan films you missed
claims: Gehri Chaal: Bachchan plays Hema Malini's brother embroiled in robbery and murder; Jeetendra is the official lead but Bachchan took the acting honours.

title: Abhimaan: A Bollywood marital drama that's relevant even after 50 years
claims: Subir's ego and jealousy when his wife outshines him; the role counted among Bachchan's finest; Saudagar was India's Oscar entry; audience readings of the envious husband.

title: 50 years of Abhimaan: When newly married Amitabh Bachchan, Jaya Bachchan shot for climax next day after returning from honeymoon
claims: Subir's jealousy at Uma's rise leads him to leave her; Bindu played Chitra.

title: Amitabh Bachchan and Nutan's Saudagar showed how women's labour is taken for granted
claims: Moti's calculated marriage to Majubi to avoid paying her wage; divorce on a false charge of infidelity; love for Phool Banu; one of Bachchan's earliest leads; reading of women's labour.

claims: Vicky's flashback structure, friendship with Somu, clash with his father, taking the blame for Somu's killing; Nisha receives Vicky from jail; women on the fringes; Bachchan has an edge over Khanna.

claims: Bachchan's 'supporting' role stole the show; commercially successful; retrospective significance for both stars; Bachchan as stoic foil in Anand.

title: Dost (1974)
claims: Bachchan has a two-minute appearance as Dharmendra's character's old friend Anand; the film ranked fourth among the year's top grossers.

title: Saat Hindustani (1969)
author: Madhulika Liddle
claims: Anwar Ali as an anti-Hindi Urdu poet from Ranchi whose house is ransacked; volunteers for the Goa mission; regarded as the group's weak link and a coward; Bachchan makes his presence felt.
notes: Used because the Wikipedia plot is one sentence.

title: Pyar Ki Kahani (1971)
claims: Ram rescues Ravi and gives him the better job; Banke's rumours about Kusum; Ram meets Kusum, learns of the gossip and accepts her; Ram's promise not to marry without Ravi's approval; Tanuja carries the film.
notes: Review withholds the ending; a reader comment describes 'a dying speech but no death'.

title: Amitabh Bachchan Retrospective: Pyar Ki Kahani, 1971
claims: Ravi is Kusum's brother who left home ashamed of the rumours; Banke spread them after Kusum spurned him; the role was intended for Jeetendra.

title: Ek Nazar (1972)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Akash is the poet son of public prosecutor Raghunath Tyagi; leaves home to continue the affair; Aminabai sells Shabnam to a Nawab; Amina is killed in a confrontation and Shabnam charged with murder, prosecuted by Tyagi.
notes: Weak source; used only for plot points consistent with the Wikipedia summary. Ending not extracted.

title: Raaste Ka Patthar (1972)
claims: Jai rescues Neeta and gets her an audition; falls in love with her while she falls for the married Choudhary, who borrows Jai's flat; Neeta Khayani billed as a newcomer; last half-hour turns grim.
notes: Review withholds the ending.

title: Bandhe Haath (1973)
claims: Shyamu's upbringing by the thief Madan; meets Mala while posing as Deepak; Mala's honesty makes him reform; Rajni's claim on Deepak and Shyamu playing along to recover the letters; Mala suspects a womaniser; the reviewer finds Bachchan aloof and uncomfortable in romantic scenes with Mumtaz.
notes: The chemistry comment is the blogger's own reply in the comments.

title: Chupke Chupke
claims: One of the most entertaining Hindi comedies; a remake of the Bengali film Chhadmabeshi; the film is dominated by Dharmendra, ably supported by Bachchan, Om Prakash, Sharmila Tagore and Jaya Bhaduri.
notes: Cited in the Chupke Chupke Wikipedia article. Publication date not captured.

title: Rajesh Khanna's Anand and Jaya Bachchan's Mili are exactly the same movie. Here's how
claims: The stubborn neighbour dealing with a personal tragedy (Shekhar) is taken by Mili's exuberance and falls in love with her; in both Anand and Mili Bachchan's character transforms from a rigid, hardened man.
notes: Cited in the Mili Wikipedia article. Publication date not captured.

title: Working it out
claims: In Chhoti Si Baat Bachchan appears as himself, arriving to seek Colonel Singh's advice on income tax while wearing his costume from Zameer; both films were produced by B. R. Chopra, and a Zameer poster appears above the film's bus stop.
notes: Title taken from the URL slug. Publication date not captured.

title: Flashback Friday: 'Alaap' Is A Musical Commentary On Society Hindi Cinema Can No Longer Create
claims: Alok is an aspiring Hindustani classical singer whose rich lawyer father tries to foil him; Rekha's Radhakumari is Ganesh's sister, both lower class; love is declared through classical song and the chemistry between Rekha and Bachchan feels natural; they share news of expecting a child; Rekha's character is merely ornamental; Bachchan's performance is restrained; the film did not do well at the box office but has aged well.
notes: Publication date not captured.

title: Amar Akbar Anthony
claims: The three heroines play second fiddle and are basically required to sing and dance; Parveen Babi looks the most fetching; the show belongs to Bachchan, whose tailor-made role has the audience in stitches.
notes: Page heading not captured; the title is the film's name. Date from the URL.

title: 100 Filmfare Days: 49- Amar Akbar Anthony
claims: Bachchan won the Filmfare Best Actor Award for the film, remembered for his mirror scene; the film etched the lost-and-found theme in Hindi film history.
notes: Publication date not captured.

title: The Tribune Spectrum, 27 August 2006
claims: Preeti Ganguli played Freni, a die-hard Amitabh Bachchan fan, in Khatta Meetha, a remake of the Lucille Ball comedy Yours, Mine and Ours.
notes: Article heading not captured; date from the URL.

title: How Kader Khan's dialogues made Devdas look cool in Muqaddar Ka Sikandar
claims: Kader Khan's dialogue lifted a conventional screenplay; the childhood bond with Kaamna echoes Devdas; Kaamna has no interest in Sikandar, a major deviation from Devdas; Zohra Begum is the film's Chandramukhi; a crowd-pleasing star vehicle for Bachchan.
notes: Title taken from the URL slug. Publication date not captured.

title: Do Anjaane (1976)
claims: Amit insists on marrying Rekha although she says she wants to dance and see the world; her success makes him insecure and he drinks and neglects her; Ranjit pushes him from a train and Rekha has no part in it; after six years of amnesia he takes revenge; his adoptive mother intervenes and Rekha is forgiven and taken home; the reviewer reads the film as condemning a career-minded woman.
notes: Plot and critical reading only. The blogger's reply in the comments adds that Rekha does not betray Amit.

title: Immaan Dharam (1977)
claims: Mohan and Ahmed give false evidence in court for money but are kind to their blind neighbour Shyamlee; Rekha's Durga is paired with Shashi Kapoor; Ahmed beats up Shyamlee's would-be rapist and gives a speech against an autopsy; the reviewer disliked the film's sermon on faith and weak script.

title: Immaan Dharam (1977)
claims: Helen's only performance as a heroine with Bachchan; the alcoholic Jenny pays Ahmed to pose as her daughter's long-lost father; when she dies of liver failure Ahmed tearfully defends her dignity; Kabir Das converts Ahmed and Mohan back to Islam and Hinduism; Durga (Rekha) is Mohan's love; the reviewers praise the film as a socially minded classic.

title: Kasme Vaade (1978)
claims: Amit and Suman delay marriage because Amit promised his mother to wait until Raju graduates; after Amit's death Raju and Suman move to Bombay; Raju befriends the car thief Shankar and burns Suman's portraits of Amit; Shankar's blood smeared on Suman's forehead symbolises marriage; the reviewers call one of Bachchan's songs 'Transcendental Bollywood'.
notes: Satirical in tone; used for plot only with Low confidence.

title: Faraar (1975)
author: Anuradha Warrier
claims: Rajesh's sister's killer is acquitted and Rajesh swears to avenge her; he takes refuge in the house of Inspector Sanjay and his wife Mala (Sharmila Tagore), whom Rajesh once saved from suicide and loved; Mala fears for her son; script and direction could have been better but the performances of the three leads are worth watching; Mala is a strong character.
notes: A commenter's reaction to the synopsis refers to Bachchan's character dying.

title: Trishul (1978)
author: Anuradha Warrier
claims: Vijay tries to bribe Geeta and she is furious; he clears her name and hires her; she is drawn to him and he depends on her; she is his support and conscience, and he turns to her for friendship, affection and love; Raakhee's Geeta has more depth than Hema Malini's role; Bachchan and Sanjeev Kumar set the screen on fire in their confrontations.

title: Don (1978)
author: Anuradha Warrier
claims: Roma, sister of a man Don killed, trains in judo and karate and infiltrates the gang; Vijay, who has begun to fall in love with her, reveals his identity when she tries to kill him, and she falls in love with him; Vijay is a street entertainer from Allahabad; the reviewer praises the zany script and calls the duet Jiska mujhe tha intezaar the only false note.

title: Zameer (1975)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Cast list naming Saira Banu's character Sunita Singh; synopsis of Badal posing as the lost son Chimpoo, falling in love with Sunita and confessing to Maharaj.
notes: The synopsis matches the Wikipedia plot almost word for word.

title: Khoon Pasina (1977)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Synopsis: Ram alias Tiger is a local criminal don who lives with his mother; he and Rekha are attracted and marry; she asks him to give up crime and he agrees; Shera is a dacoit and rival.
notes: Names Bachchan's character Ram; Wikipedia calls him Shiva.

title: Besharam (1978)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Synopsis: Ramchandra is framed after winning a mayoral election and hangs himself; the Prince Chandrashekar from Johannesburg romances both Digvijay's sister Renuka and Manju.

title: Benaam (1974)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Synopsis: Amit and Sheela see the reporter Mr. Verma stabbed; threatening calls follow; their son Rajoo disappears. Trivia: Amit Srivastav is Bachchan's real family name.

title: Ganga Ki Saugandh (1978): A Microcosm Representing Indian Society in a Nutshell
claims: Jeeva lives with his widowed mother Ramvati and is fond of Dhaniya (Rekha), daughter of Kalu Chamar (Pran); the Thakur tries to molest Dhaniya; the villagers under Kalu refuse Jeeva's help once he is a criminal; the film as a picture of Indian society.

title: 11 films where Rajinikanth acted in an Amitabh Bachchan remake and aced them
claims: Billa (1980) was a remake of Don; Dharmathin Thalaivan was a remake of Kasme Vaade; both starred Rajinikanth.
notes: Cited in the Khoon Pasina Wikipedia article. Publication date not captured.

title: Sulakshana Pandit
claims: Filmography table: Hera Pheri (1976), role Asha, co-star Vinod Khanna.
notes: Used only to identify which lead each actress is paired with in Hera Pheri.

title: Deewar had the best screenplay ever, says Amitabh Bachchan
claims: On the film's 42nd anniversary Bachchan called Deewaar 'the best screenplay ever' and recalled its 100-week trophy; the film established him as the angry young man.
notes: Month inferred from 'clocked 42 years today' and the January 1975 release.

title: Why Hrishida made happy films
claims: Hrishikesh Mukherjee recalled that some people thought he had blundered by making Bachchan sing classical songs in Alaap when other directors had him holding guns and booze bottles.
notes: Date from the URL.

title: Silsila: Pretty nothingness (film review)
author: Sunil Sethi
claims: Contemporary review: calls the film 'pure polyester yarn'; says Chopra 'reconventionalised' adultery for public taste; Amit marries Jaya's character to save her from ostracism and returns to her at the end; Bachchan's sacrifice and seduction are 'as synthetic as his tiresome chauvinism'; the ending is an 'affirmation of marriage'.
notes: Full text read from the article body in the cached page.

title: Film review: Yaarana, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Amjad Khan, Neetu Singh
author: A. P.
claims: Contemporary review: two standard Bachchan routines, the rustic in the city and the pop star, 'done to perfection'; Neetu Singh gives 'a little romantic encouragement' as his teacher's daughter; the plot 'goes berserk' after the concert; remembered, if at all, for hang-gliding.
notes: Full text read from the article body in the cached page.

title: Film review: Satte Pe Satta, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Hema Malini, Amjad Khan
author: Jagannath Dubashi
claims: Contemporary review: a copy of Seven Brides for Seven Brothers whose first half is 'a satisfying duplicate'; the wife 'sets house and brothers to rights'; Babu 'falls for her with a thud'; an excellent Amjad Khan–Bachchan scene; the double role misses a chance to take Bachchan out of his rut.
notes: Full text read from the article body in the cached page.

title: Film review: Khud-daar, starring Sanjeev Kumar, Amitabh Bachchan, Vinod Mehra, Parveen Babi
author: S. Venkat Narayan
claims: Contemporary review: 'an Amitabh film from beginning to the end' with a stronger emotional appeal than Dostana, Yarana, Shaan, Desh Premee and Kaalia; the hero reforms nearly everyone, including Parveen Babi's Christian girl who gives up an illicit liquor trade to win him over.
notes: Full text read from the article body in the cached page.

title: Year 1981 was for Indian movies what 1977 had been for Indian politics
author: Sunil Sethi
claims: Naseeb and Kranti were 'price-tagged at over Rs 4 crore each'; Bachchan's bravura paid off in Laawaris and Yaarana but palled in Barsaat Ki Ek Raat; Silsila was 'the silliest damp squib of the year'; Bachchan 'changed four pairs of bosoms in Laawaris and was booed'; Chashme Buddoor became a milestone as a classy comedy that drew full houses.
notes: Read from the article body in the cached page.

title: Satte Pe Satta: a fun treat!
author: Gaurav Sharma
claims: Retrospective: a musical comedy in a commercial format; Indu is Ravi's love; Babu has a change of heart and finds love with the woman he was sent to kill; 'right doses of humour, music and action'.

title: English is a very funny language—Bachchan gave the OG Bollywood monologue in 'Namak Halaal'
author: Triya Gulati
claims: Kader Khan wrote the English monologue; Smita Patil plays Poonam; 'Aaj Rapat Jaayen To' was her first Bollywood-style dance number; reports say she went home and cried after the shoot; Bachchan persuaded her and wrote in 2016 that she was uncomfortable throughout.

title: When Amitabh Bachchan put an 'uncomfortable' Smita Patil at ease during Namak Halal
author: Entertainment Desk
claims: Namak Halaal at 40: Smita Patil, known for art-house work, had to lip-sync and dance to 'Aaj Rapat Jaye' with Bachchan; the soundtrack is described as iconic.

title: Amitabh Bachchan on 36 years of Yaarana: It still resounds among polity of the nation
author: IANS
claims: Bachchan said shooting 'Sara Zamana' in a Kolkata stadium and the lit jacket were his ideas, and that the film still resounds among the polity.

title: Basu Chatterjee's Gentle, Middle-Of-The-Road Cinema Was That Of The People Next Door
author: Baradwaj Rangan
claims: Manzil is 'surely the only Hindi film with galvanometers in the plot'; its protagonist dreams of becoming an entrepreneur; the critic singles out its melodramatic concluding portions.
notes: The kept paragraph was cut off mid-sentence after 'melodramatic concluding portions of Manzil'.

title: Did you know this about Amitabh Bachchan?
claims: Bachchan went uncredited for his role of a Punjabi truck driver in the Amjad Khan starrer Commander (1981), to help a friend.

title: Ramesh Sippy on casting Amitabh Bachchan and Dilip Kumar together in Shakti
author: Subhash K. Jha
claims: Interview: Sippy worked on Shaan and Shakti after Sholay; he wanted to make a 'Father India' with Dilip Kumar about a man who sacrifices his son for his ideology.
notes: Primary interview published by an entertainment site.

title: Amitabh Bachchan turns nostalgic as Barsaat Ki Ek Raat completes 37 years of release
claims: Quotes Bachchan's tweet: the Bengali version Anusandhan was the top-grossing Bengali film; 1981 had four 'Super Blockbusters' (Naseeb, Lawaaris, Yaraana, Kaalia); Silsila is 'a cult film now'.
source_type: News agency story quoting the actor
notes: The box-office claims are Bachchan's own and conflict with Box Office India's verdicts; used only as his statement.

title: The champion of masala films, Manmohan Desai made Bollywood what it is today
author: Madhavi Pothukuchi
claims: Desai and Bachchan made some of the biggest hits of both their careers together: Naseeb, Coolie, Desh Premee.

title: Cinema Cinema (film review)
claims: The film assembles extracts supposedly watched by stereotyped viewers in a sleazy cinema and has 'semi-sociological pretensions'.
notes: No date or author on the page.

title: 50 Years of Hindi Alternative Cinema
author: Uday Bhatia; Jai Arjun Singh
claims: Cinema Cinema (1979): a 'charming history lesson, presented as a faux movie screening', covering Hindi cinema from the silents to the 1970s, with cameos by Dharmendra and Hema Malini.

title: Scene of the Week : Chashme Buddoor
author: sputnik
claims: Chashme Buddoor includes 'a breezy appearance by Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha' and a parody of hit songs.

title: Ahsaas: Kooky film, cool t-shirts
claims: Surindara Suri's Ahsaas (1979) was backed by G. P. Sippy and featured top stars such as Amitabh Bachchan, Shashi Kapoor, Amjad Khan and Bindiya Goswami.

title: Manzil (1979)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)

notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Conversations Over Chai: Kaala Patthar (1979)
author: Anuradha Warrier
claims: Vijay meets Dr Sudha Sen at the clinic, where he refuses anaesthesia; she shares her story and they slowly fall in love; the romance is 'very subtle and understated, very much like their romance in Trishul'.

title: Conversations Over Chai: Suhaag (1979)
author: Anuradha Warrier
claims: Amit loves Basanti (Rekha), the local nautch girl, and keeps urging her to leave the business and marry him; she is Annu's sister; Rekha 'had great chemistry' with Bachchan and was 'a great masala heroine'.

title: Conversations Over Chai: Naseeb (1981)
author: Anuradha Warrier
claims: Johnny rescues Asha from Ashok; their romance flourishes with 'complete understanding'; Johnny and Julie make 'the ultimate sacrifice', leaving Asha furious; Asha later understands, and Vicky hands her over to Johnny.

title: Conversations Over Chai: The Great Gambler (1979)
author: Anuradha Warrier
claims: Ratan Das treats Jai as a son and sends him to marry Deepchand's heiress Mala; Saxena sends Romesh's girlfriend Shabnam to make Jai fall for her; Jai flirts with Shabnam but later treats her with contempt; Mala declares her love to Vijay, who leaves her a note confessing he is not Jai.

title: Desh Premee (1982)
author: Memsaab
claims: Raju, working for Pratap Singh as 'Tony', hides from police in a group wedding with the cabaret dancer Asha, who treats it as a lifelong commitment; he spends the wedding night with her and disappears; Masterji's integrity 'both destroys his happiness and saves his loved ones at the end'.

title: Do Aur Do Paanch (1980)
claims: Ram catches the eye of Parveen Babi's character and Lakshman that of Hema Malini's; both actresses are 'relegated to the most menial of supporting roles'.

title: Mr Natwarlal (1979)
claims: Natwar was raised by his brother and sister-in-law; Shanno sets her cap at him; he rescues her and she rescues him on several occasions; Rekha and Bachchan's chemistry is 'always wonderful'; Natwar learns to love something more than himself.

title: Laawaris Film Review
claims: Heera comes across Mohini, a privileged woman, 'and of course stalks her to show his affection'; she is the girl who once gave him a book; when she learns who he is they share a song.

title: Film review: Andhaa Kaanoon is what they call a masala film
author: S. Venkat Narayan
claims: Bachchan plays an honest forest officer jailed for 20 years for a murder he did not commit; his wife (Madhavi) is dishonoured by goondas, throttles their daughter and kills herself. After release he chases the forest contractor (Amrish Puri) into the courtroom and stabs him before the judge who convicted him. Bachchan 'appears content playing a secondary role'; the court scene is 'one of the most gripping and memorable on the Hindi screen'; he 'shows his flair for comedy in a song sequence in which he cajoles his wife in vain to plant a kiss on his cheek'. He reportedly charged Rs 1 lakh a day. The reviewer predicts a blockbuster.
notes: Magazine issue of 30 April 1983, republished online in 2013; text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Manmohan Desai and Prakash Mehra stand out as remarkable survivors with big budget films
author: Sumit Mitra
claims: Coolie was made at a cost of Rs 2 crore and netted Rs 3.5 crore from the sale of distribution rights before its 2 December 1983 release; it had passed Rs 1 crore in the Bombay territory and earned at least Rs 80 lakh in every major territory. Sharaabi was pre-sold at Rs 35 lakh per major territory. Describes the shooting of Mard, with Bachchan as the anti-imperialist champion of the underdog.
notes: Text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Release of Amitabh Bachchan film 'Shahenshah' delayed
author: M. Rahman
claims: Tinnu Anand signed Bachchan in 1983; his illness delayed shooting to late 1985. Meenakshi Sheshadri replaced Dimple Kapadia as heroine. The film was completed in October 1987 at an estimated cost of Rs 2.5 crore. Distribution rights were first sold at Rs 45 lakh per territory, then offered outright at a reported Rs 90 lakh per territory.
notes: Magazine issue of 31 January 1988, republished online in 2013.

title: Amitabh Bachchan makes spectacular come-back with Shahenshah
author: Simran Bhargava
claims: Released on 12 February 1988 amid threats from opposition youth wings, with record advance booking. The film is 'a rehash of everything Amitabh has ever done' and 'a long, somewhat irritating film with a familiar taste'. By day Bachchan plays a crude paan-chewing policeman, by night Shahenshah; Meenakshi Seshadri is 'the fresh, leggy heroine who lives in a slum'. The hero 'gets a beautiful woman's love'. In the finale he drives a truck into the courtroom and hangs the villain.
notes: Text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Amitabh Bachchan's future looks uncertain as 'Ganga Jamuna Saraswati' bombs
author: Salil Tripathi
claims: Released on 23 December 1988 in 270 theatres, the film 'had bombed' within a fortnight. Distributors paid up to Rs 75 lakh per territory. First-week Bombay collections were Rs 12.76 lakh (95 per cent of potential); in the second week revenue fell to 28–40 per cent. Critic Iqbal Masud called it 'trite and boring'; Bombay distributor Puran Chandra Rao said 'Amitabh has miserably disappointed'. Toofan's February release was postponed. Bachchan's new films included Jadugar, Toofan and Tinnu Anand's Satyam.
notes: Text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Film of the Month: Amitabh's Agneepath is more than mere Scarface, maloom?
author: Shaikh Ayaz
claims: Agneepath 'was an epic flop on release', 'trashed as a middling Scarface copy', and is now 'an oft-quoted cult film'. Vijay Dinanath Chavan is 'by far the most wounded' of Bachchan's Vijays, and the film is full of homage to the Bachchan mythology.
notes: Fetched with curl; only paragraphs about Bachchan and the film's reception were kept.

title: Cinemascoop: how reporters have fared in Hindi films
author: Vikramdeep Johal
claims: Shabana Azmi is 'flawless' in Main Azaad Hoon as the opportunistic columnist who creates a man of the masses to raise her paper's circulation; Azaad's sincerity gives her pangs of conscience and leads to a clash with her bosses. The film is a remake of Frank Capra's Meet John Doe.
notes: Title taken from the section heading; the page has no headline tag.

title: Coolie (1983)
claims: Julie (Rati Agnihotri) is the heiress ward of Puri, who wants her to marry Vicky for her fortune; she resists because she wants to avenge her father's death first. The coolies crash the engagement party and Iqbal carts Julie off as a hostage; 'it's pretty much love at first sight', though she escapes after tying him up.
notes: Read through the WordPress.com API; only paragraphs about Julie were kept.

title: Ajooba (1991)
claims: Rukhsana (Dimple Kapadia), Amir Khan's grown daughter, travels alone to Bahrestan to find her imprisoned father; Prince Altaf seizes her, Ajooba rescues her and she gives him a silver bracelet; bandits then kidnap her from Hassan's horse and auction her.
notes: Read through the WordPress.com API; only paragraphs about Rukhsana were kept.

title: Mard (1985)
claims: Raju meets Ruby, Dr Harry's spoiled heiress daughter, and 'sparks - and salt - and whips - fly'; the reviewers call the couple's 'sadomasochistic romp, complete with whipping and rubbing salt in each other's wounds' baffling. Ruby is sent off to marry Danny. Amrita Singh 'generally matched her macho boytoy' in gutsy action, apart from 'silly, coy, and helpless' routines; the film is 'the Amitabh Bachchan show'.
notes: Read from the Blogger feed; only paragraphs about Ruby and the performances were kept.

title: Mahaan (1983)
claims: Amit, a lawyer, exposes his friend Vikram as a drug smuggler; Vikram later frames him for murder and Amit hides in Nepal as Rana Ranveersingh. Janki raises Shankar, who becomes a police inspector, and an orphan girl Manju, who loves Shankar. Guru is raised by a foster couple and loves song, dance and drama; Reeta asks him for a fake marriage to satisfy her grandfather Rai Sahab and later falls in love with him. The film flopped.
notes: Read from the Blogger feed. It says Janki raises Manju; Wikipedia calls Manju Rana Ranveer's adopted daughter.

title: Mahaan (1983): a blend of action, melodrama, with exaggerated emotions and dialogue
author: Shreya Raolji
claims: The narrative revolves around Amit and his wife Janki, torn apart by his school friend Vikram Singh's betrayal; Vikram frames Amit for Rajan's murder. Bachchan transitions seamlessly between Amit, Guru and Inspector Shankar.
notes: Fetched with curl; only paragraphs about the characters were kept.

notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed. The synopsis confuses Vikram and Amit in one sentence.

He helps the authorities catch Shekhar, the Police Commissioner's killer, then sets out to kill Shekhar's parents and learns who they are and why Purandare shot his father.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Coolie (1983)

Pregnant Asha discovers he is a pawn of politicians using him as a hit man. Trivia: working title 'Amar Akbar Anthony part 2'.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Toofan (1989)

Shyam goes to their village to avenge him and is mistaken for Toofan, a man with powers blessed by Hanuman who has disappeared. Trivia: 'Aaya Toofan' was Kishore Kumar's last song for a Bachchan film.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed. Its cast list names only Bachchan, Meenakshi Seshadri and Amrita Singh, and it does not mention a romance.

Trivia: working title Satyam; Subhashini stops him saying his real name; a Kolkata fan jumped from a cinema balcony imitating the death scene.

title: Hum (1991)

Years later, as Shekhar, he learns that Jumma has become a famous actress shooting in Bangalore.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed. It names Vijay's girlfriend Neeta; Wikipedia's cast list says Anita.

title: The smiles that fail to enthuse (review of Tere Mere Sapne)
author: Anupama Chopra
claims: The first ABCL film is 'an average product': a prince-and-pauper trading-places tale introducing Chandrachur Singh, Arshad Warsi and Priya Gill. Singh is endearing; Gill is 'irritatingly coy'. ABCL is 'a far more innovative distributor than maker'. The review does not mention Bachchan's narration.
notes: Text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Movies (capsule reviews: Major Saab, Devil's Advocate, Mercury Rising)
claims: The Indian army has objected to the NDA-set film and Bachchan has defended factual errors as 'only a movie'. An army major and cadets try to unite two lovers; 'The script is full of loopholes. The Big B is angry - nothing new. Devgan is sincere and Bendre insipid. Waste of talent.'
notes: No author given. The URL carries the issue date 1998-07-13; the JSON-LD date is 1998-08-10.

title: South Indian actress Soundarya debuts in Bollywood with Sooryavansham
claims: Sooryavansham is the Bollywood debut of Bachchan's co-star Soundarya, 22, who had made 65 Tamil, Telugu and Kannada films.
notes: Text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Two's a crowd (review of Kohram)
author: Anupama Chopra
claims: Kohram has 'Krantiveer-like crude energy'; the first half moves fast with Bachchan and Patekar as army men in a cat-and-mouse game, but the second half slows. The colonel (Bachchan) misses a corrupt politician three times; Patekar's major pursues him disguised as a stammering photo-journalist; Tabu's corrupt inspector falls for Patekar. Bachchan, 'breathing fire and brimstone as the colonel and playing comedy as a Banaras ka bhaiya, partially recreates the old magic. But he looks haggard and weary to the bone.'
notes: Text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Many Indian Movies in One
author: Stephen Holden
claims: Review of Khuda Gawah: Bachchan, 'an Indian superstar who outthunders Charlton Heston and outglares Rudolph Valentino', plays Badshah Khan, 'a heroic patriarch' bound by his word, and proclaims his lines 'in a deep impassioned roar'. 'As he locks eyes with Sridevi, the actress who plays his wife, Benazir, the screen is in danger of melting.' Badshah is beaten, tortured, imprisoned, shot at and bombed; for 18 years Benazir mumbles 'He will return'. Sridevi also plays the couple's daughter.
notes: Read from a 2016 Wayback Machine copy; the live page returns no article text to curl.

title: Bachchan's feat of clay
claims: Mrityudaata, 'touted as his comeback vehicle and a lifesaver for his floundering company, ABCL, has run aground': 90 per cent collections in Mumbai for three days, then a crash, with first-week averages across India under 70 per cent. Audiences looking for the angry young man found he had aged. A Mid-day poll placed Bachchan fifth among the 10 most-hated people. He reportedly chose Mehul Kumar over Govind Nihalani and Shekhar Kapur.
notes: No author given; archive page.

title: The preview, slide show and real video file of Major Saab
claims: Major Jasbir Singh Rana, played by Bachchan, is 'one of those officers with a stony exterior and heart full of mush'; he decides not to boot out the recalcitrant cadet but keeps an eye on him and comes to his aid. Shot at the NDA, in Australia and Bombay; Bachchan plays his age.
notes: Pre-release preview, not a review. Date from the URL.

title: The Bade Miyan Chote Miyan review
claims: Arjun Singh (Bachchan) and Pyare Mohan (Govinda) are police friends; Arjun's sister Seema loves Pyare; Arjun 'has no female companion and some pretty crude comments are often passed about his age'. Neha (Ramya Krishnan) is a second eyewitness. Madhuri Dixit appears as herself. 'The film that's supposed to establish Amitabh's supremacy fails miserably'; as with Shakti, one star overshadows the other, 'here, it was just Govinda doing the overshadowing'.
notes: Author not identified on the page.

title: The review of K C Bokadia's Lal Badshah
claims: Bachchan plays a double role of father and son, speaks a north Indian rural dialect, stars opposite Manisha Koirala and Shilpa Shetty, has Nirupa Roy as his mother again and does a drunk dance. The older character guarded the treasury. Koirala plays a life insurance agent who falls for the hero; Shetty plays lawyer Mohan Joshi's daughter. 'Bachchan is a natural with comedy, he can sleepwalk through the ma-beta bits, he can look convincing as a saviour.'
notes: Author not identified on the page.

title: The review of Mehul Kumar's Kohram
author: Sharmila Taliculam
claims: Colonel Balbir Singh Sodhi (Bachchan) fails to kill minister Virbhadra Singh. 'It's a pleasure seeing Nana Patekar and Amitabh Bachchan together for the first time.' Bachchan is understated and times his lines well in his Bihari accent, but Patekar is handed the better lines. Tabu and Nana have 'a strange chemistry'. Jaya Prada comes on screen after a long time.
notes: The author is named by Wikipedia's Kohram article, not on the fetched page.

title: Ek Rishtaa (Bond of Love) review
author: Dharmesh Rajput
claims: Bachchan plays 'the mature and mellow Vijay Kapoor who has worked from nothing to create an industrial empire' and sticks to strong principles; his relationship with his newly graduated son (Akshay Kumar) is the film's main thrust. 'The real pleasure of this film is Amitabh's performance.'
notes: Date from the URL.

title: The film review of Ek Rishtaa-The Bond of Love
author: Savera R Someshwar
claims: Vijay Kapoor (Bachchan) is a successful, kind businessman with wife Pratima (Rakhee), three daughters and son Ajay. 'There is no depth to the relationship between Amitabh and Rakhee'; 'Rakhee has been completely wasted in this bit role.' Praises the climax, where the villain faces 'the cold rage of an avenging Amitabh', and the father–son confrontation.
notes: The author is named by Wikipedia's article, not on the fetched text.

title: Aks review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Synopsis: Manu Verma (Bachchan) is head of security for the Indian Defence Minister on a Budapest visit; he reaches the minister moments too late after the assassin Raghavan strikes, becomes 'a man obsessed with capturing Raghavan', and catches him.
notes: Only the synopsis paragraphs matched; the rating (2/5) is from the page title.

title: The Rediff Review: Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham
author: Anjum N
claims: Strict businessman Yashovardhan (Bachchan) and his 'compliant, loving wife Nandini (Jaya Bachchan)'. Bachchan plays opposite Jaya 'after 16 years and for the first time as old parents'; he sings 'Aati Kya Khandala' for Jaya at his birthday party. 'Amitabh delivers a controlled performance, yet again'; Jaya 'performs as well as she has always does, especially opposite her husband'. Yashovardhan apologises to his sons at the end.
notes: The author is named by Wikipedia's article, not on the fetched text.

title: A guide to Aankhen
claims: 'Apart from his good-cop-turned-evil-doer act in Aks, Amitabh Bachchan plays the villain after nearly 30 years.'
notes: Pre-release guide; date from the URL.

title: The Rediff Review: Hum Kisise Kum Nahin
claims: Munna Bhai is taken to reputed shrink Doctor Rastogi (Bachchan); Rastogi and Komal go to Malaysia, where she is to be engaged to the son of the doctor's former classmate. Bachchan and Sanjay Dutt 'keep the viewers engaged in the beginning but they irritate post-intermission'.
notes: Author not identified in the fetched text.

title: Hum Kisise Kum Nahin
author: Manish Gajjar
claims: Munnabhai is taken to psychiatrist Dr Rastogi (Amitabh) and later discovers the true relationship between Rastogi and Komal. 'As Dr Rastogi he is once again at his comic best.' Ajay Devgan surprises with a versatile comic performance.
notes: Month from the URL.

title: The Rediff Review: Agni Varsha
claims: 'The real disappointment is Amitabh Bachchan, who has a much-hyped appearance as Lord Indra.'
notes: Author not identified in the fetched text.

title: Review: Kaante
claims: Rating 3.5 stars. Major (Amitabh), Ajju, Marc, Andy, Baali and Mak plan one gigantic heist. 'Amitabh Bachchan is, as always, sincere and delivers the goods well.'
notes: Read from a 2005 Wayback Machine copy; no author or date on the page.

title: Kaante
author: Derek Elley
claims: Yashvardhan 'Major' Rampal (Bachchan) 'is a former gangster who tried to go straight and has a dying wife at home'. Gupta directs the film primarily as a character piece, 'with Bachchan, Dutt and semi-comic relief Manjrekar driving the drama with richly characterized roles'.

title: Armaan: Philanthropy, love et al
claims: Dr Sinha (Bachchan) 'refuses to become cynical or indifferent despite the struggles he faces and the death and diseases he lives amidst'. Honey Irani 'has brought out some of the best moments in Amitabh Bachchan's and Anil Kapoor's career'; 'one, however, still wonders why Amitabh was given that helpless look'.
notes: Read from a 2005 Wayback Machine copy; no author or date on the page.

title: Akka (1994)
claims: Akka, directed by Shridhar Joshi, features Ajay Fhansekar, Sulabha Deshpande, Prashant Damle and Amitabh Bachchan. Bachchan's make-up artist Deepak Sawant produced it and wanted him to introduce the film; Bachchan insisted on acting, so a song sequence was added to the completed film. The song had been recorded in a female voice, so Jaya Bachchan was asked to perform too; the devotional theme number 'Tu Jagati Adhipati' was reshot with both.
notes: Search-result summary only; it draws on IMDb and https://akka-1994.bollyviews.com/, and neither page was fetched.

title: Indrajeet (1991)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Synopsis: honest police officer Indrajeet must arrest his girlfriend Shanti's father, Seth Din Dayal; 'when his girlfriend stands up for her father, Indrajeet gets offended'. Years later the retired Indrajeet arranges his adopted daughter Neelu's marriage to Vijay, and both are killed by Shanti's brother.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Insaniyat (1994)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Bachchan was first signed for a guest appearance but was given a full role during production, becoming the lead. The makers gave away the jacket he wore as a promotion. The film was delayed from 1991, was his last before his temporary retirement from 1992, and failed.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Mrityudaata (1997)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Produced by ABCL. Dr Ram Prasad Ghayal lives with his wife Janaki (Dimple) and brother Bharat, and sets out 'to avenge the loss of his wife and his brother'. The film marked Bachchan's comeback after a six-year sabbatical. Bachchan heard Daler Mehndi at a wedding and had him record a song when the film was 90–95 per cent complete.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Major Saab (1998)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Produced by Bachchan. The release was delayed a week because the Indian Army objected to Bachchan's beard; the opening credits cite the Army's policy on beards. Abhishek Bachchan was an uncredited assistant.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Bade Miyan Chote Miyan (1998)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Bachchan plays Inspector Arjun Singh and Bade Miyan. Neha (Ramya Krishnan), who sees her friend killed, calls the station for Pyare; Arjun goes instead and masquerades as Pyare. The thieves are mistaken for Arjun and Pyare by Seema and Neha; Zorawar kidnaps Seema and demands the diamond and Neha.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Lal Baadshah (1999)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Cast: Bachchan as Lal 'Baadshah' Singh and Ranbhir Singh; Manisha Koirala as Kiran, a life insurance agent; Raadhika Sarathkumar as Ranbhir Singh's wife. Kiran falls in love with Lal and is determined to become his wife. Koirala took the film to work with Bachchan.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Sooryavansham (1999)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Thakur Bhanupratap Singh (Bachchan) is enraged when his son Heera (Bachchan) proposes to marry his childhood sweetheart Gauri, and more so when Heera backs down, promising never to marry; unknown to the father, Gauri refused an illiterate husband. Radha (Soundarya) loves Heera for his gentle manner and proposes; they leave the village, and he becomes a successful businessman and she a government officer.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed. Wikipedia instead says Bhanupratap arranged the Heera–Gauri marriage.

title: Hindustan Ki Kasam (1999)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: ABCL was first to produce the film. Bachchan's Kabeera was written loosely as a sutradhar (narrator), 'a man of no particular religion who speaks his mind'.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Kohram (1999)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Produced by ABCL. Jaya Prada plays Colonel Sodhi's wife Namrata; Tabu is a police officer in love with Major Ajit Arya. Mehul Kumar's project was first titled 'Aye Watan Tere Liye' with Bachchan, Dimple Kapadia, Arshad Warsi and Karisma Kapoor; Bachchan kept his commitment despite Mrityudaata's failure.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Aks (2001)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Produced by Bachchan and distributed by ABCL. At 58 Bachchan jumped 30 feet with Manoj Bajpayee for the waterfall scene. Nandita Das said at a press conference that her finished role was the opposite of what had been explained to her.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Aankhen (2002)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: The film had two endings: in the Indian one Bachchan's character repents and is locked away; in the overseas one he bribes the police. Bachchan returned to negative roles with this film.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Boom review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Saleem (Gulshan Grover) answers to Bade Mia (Bachchan), 'the kingpin, the father-figure and the most notorious gangster on India's Most Wanted list', and 'Bade Mia wants the diamonds back, come what may!' The action shifts to Bachchan, Grover and Zeenat Aman in Dubai. The critic wonders what Bachchan saw in 'an insipid role'; 'the veteran has a substantial role', but the director 'has wasted' him.
notes: Rating 1/5 from the page title.

title: Kerchief caper!
author: Seema Pant
claims: What sets Baghban apart is 'the on-going romance between the lead couple': Raj (Bachchan) and Puja (Hema Malini) 'are very much in love even after 40 years of marriage' and 'romance, sing and dance'. Raj gives his sons the last of his savings. When each son agrees to keep one parent for six months, Raj warns Puja, 'They want to separate us, not share our love', but defers to her; neither is happy apart, and the children ill-treat them. Alok loves them unconditionally, and the Patels become important in Raj's life. 'The film belongs to Amitabh Bachchan and Hema Malini. He sings, dances, romances, cries and makes you cry.'
notes: Rediff spells Hema Malini's character Puja; Wikipedia has Pooja.

title: Baghban review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: At his farewell party Raj Malhotra (Bachchan) announces that he wants to spend the rest of his life with his wife. Memorable scenes include Lilette Dubey reading Hema's letter to Amitabh after he breaks his glasses, and the climax, where 'Amitabh's oration' on the parent-child relationship 'is brilliant'. 'Amitabh Bachchan delivers a wonderful performance. Hema Malini looks elegant and conveys the pathos convincingly.'
notes: Wikipedia reports a two-star rating.

title: Khakee is money's worth. What more do you want?
author: Sukanya Verma
claims: 'At the fag end of his career, DCP Anant Shrivastava (Amitabh Bachchan) is finally asked to go on a life-threatening mission', having waited 'for an opportunity to prove his guts'; it comes as he and his wife (Jaya Prada) prepare for their daughter's wedding. 'Through DCP Anant Shrivastava, Santoshi expresses his anger at corruption, admonishes the media and the easily influenced masses.' Bachchan 'portrays his Anant Shrivastava with determination and grace'.

title: Khakee review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: The assignment is given to DCP Anant (Bachchan). Highlights: his pre-interval argument with Akshay Kumar, his argument with the villain, 'Amitabh's outburst at the police station, when he reminds the Officer Incharge of the duties of men in uniform', and the finale in which 'Amitabh and the villain come to blows'. 'In KHAKEE, Amitabh Bachchan delivers one of the best performances of his career.'
notes: Rating 4/5 from the page title.

title: So what's the deal about Aetbaar?
author: Gaurav Sharma
claims: A remake of Fear. The plot 'revolves around a small family of three with Amitabh (Dr Ranvir) as the head and Bipasha (Ria) as the daughter'; 'the rest of the plot is for the father to convince his daughter about Aryan's reality and to get even with him'. Bachchan sings a track. 'Slow and not at all gripping, not even when the father decides to go after Aryan.'

title: Aetbaar review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Aetbaar is about 'an over-possessive father out to save his daughter from the clutches of her weird lover'. Malhotra (Bachchan) 'believes he's simply a protective parent, while his daughter Ria believes he's simply possessive'; Aryan is 'the epitome of all the values that Ria's father abhors'.
notes: Rating 3/5 from the page title.

title: Dev: what's the fuss all about?
author: Vivek Fernandes
claims: Joint Police Commissioner Dev Pratap Singh (Bachchan) 'believes in serving and protecting the interests of the nation above all else' and is 'pigeonholed as a Muslim-hater'; his only son, aged 5, was killed by a bullet, and attempts have been made on his life and that of his wife, Dr Bharati (Rati Agnihotri). His friend of over 30 years, Special Commissioner Tejinder Khosla (Om Puri), turns bad; 'the scenes involving Bachchan and Puri make for the most riveting parts'. Farhan, who has tried to kill Dev, finally turns to him.

title: India Today's Kaveree Bamzai reviews film Dev by Govind Nihalani
author: Kaveree Bamzai
claims: 'One of the best things to have happened to post millennial Bollywood is the ageing of Amitabh Bachchan.' Dev is possibly 'the most brutal look at communal riots in mainstream cinema so far'. 'Bachchan is like the Glenfiddich he and Om Puri drink: impeccable and elegant.'
notes: Text from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Dev review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'DEV is about Dev [Amitabh Bachchan] and Tej's [Om Puri] friendship', 'a bond stronger than blood ties'; their conversations 'veer into a sermonizing mood'. 'It would be difficult to imagine anyone except Amitabh Bachchan enacting the title role.' 'Rati Agnihotri is competent.'
notes: Rating 2/5 from the page title.

title: Lakshya review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan doesn't get much scope, but his work is commendable. His dialogue in Marathi will meet with a thunderous response in Maharashtra.'
notes: Rating 2.5/5 from the page title.

title: Deewaar: Let's Bring Our Heroes Home
author: Derek Elley
claims: Major Kaul (Bachchan, 'in full Alec Guinness Kwai mode') has been 'rotting in a Pakistani POW camp for the past 33 years but still dreaming of returning to India'; the film opens with his 18th escape attempt. 'Kaul's wife, Nanda (Tanuja), never stopped believing he was alive, but his son, Gaurav, long ago lost hope.' The opening reels dwell on 'Kaul's physical humiliation by his leering Pakistani captors and his stiff-backed resistance'.
notes: Variety spells the character Ranbir.

title: Deewaar review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Gaurav decides to bring his father, Major Ranvir Kaul (Bachchan), back home, aided by Khan. 'It is Amitabh Bachchan who towers above all with a splendid and power-packed performance'; it is his third memorable performance of the year, after Khakee and Dev.
notes: Wikipedia reports a 3/5 rating.

title: Kyun! Ho Gaya Na review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Malhotra's dear friend Raj Chauhan (Bachchan) 'has dedicated his life to a small orphanage he runs at his home'. Amitabh enters at the intermission, when the story shifts to the orphanage children, whose pranks 'fall flat'. 'Even the climax, when Amitabh reveals his game-plan, does not have the desired impact. Amitabh Bachchan is extremely likeable.'

title: Why is Amitabh in Hum Kaun Hai?
author: Malishka Mendonsa
claims: The posters showed Bachchan as the leading man, but 'Amitabh, in fact, has an extended guest appearance. He is like a poster boy, trying to attract the audiences.' Dimple Kapadia plays an overprotective mother of two photosensitive children.

title: Hum Kaun Hai review
author: Manish Gajjar
claims: Sandra's husband, Major Frank John Williams (Bachchan), is at war with no news of his return; on her way through the woods Sandra bumps into Frank, who, with his friend Virendra (Dharmendra), 'begins to investigate the mystery surrounding his family'. 'Amitabh Bachchan makes a special appearance in the film even though the publicity showed him as the central character.'
notes: Published September 2004 per the URL path; the page gives no exact date.

title: Ab Tumhare Hawale is a muddle!
author: Patcy N
claims: After Vikramjit (Bobby Deol) dies for the nation, his son Kunal is 'forced to join the army by his grandfather (Amitabh Bachchan)'. 'Amitabh talks about his son Bobby proving himself in the war', then ends 'mouthing clichés about always wanting peace'. 'Amitabh Bachchan is seen far too often in these officer roles and has nothing at all new to offer in this uniformed outing.'

title: Ab Tumhare Hawale Watan Sathiyo review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: The film 'tells the story of Amarjeet Singh [Amitabh Bachchan], an army officer, who watches his son Vikramjeet Singh [Bobby Deol] sacrifice his life for the nation'. 'Amitabh Bachchan breathes fire when he confronts his opponents.'

title: With 'Black', Sanjay Leela Bhansali attempts a monochromatic leap forward for Indian cinema
claims: Bachchan calls Black 'the most exhausting film he has ever made'. 'The movie belongs to Bachchan and Rani Mukherji, both of whom spent six months learning sign language for the blind.' Bhansali 'marvels at the way Bachchan uses the power of silence'.
notes: Text from the page's JSON-LD articleBody; no byline in the extract.

title: Black: Bhansali's passion, pain and pleasure
author: Sita Menon
claims: Debraj Sahai (Bachchan) 'wrangles himself into the responsibility of turning the blind, deaf and mute girl into a fine young lady'; Michelle's father fumes at 'the drunk, ill-mannered teacher'. The review notes comic touches, such as Bachchan swearing in sign language, and the late scene in which 'Debraj stretches Michelle's hand out the window and into the rain'.
notes: URL not cited in the Wikipedia article; found by Rediff's date pattern.

title: Waqt loses the race
author: Vishal D'Souza
claims: Ishwarchand Thakur (Bachchan) is a 'postman-turned-toy maker and industrialist' who 'dotes devotedly on Adi who can do no wrong, much to the dismay of his wife (Shefali Shah)'. He sends Aditya packing because he 'hides a deep painful secret that he cannot yet share with Aditya'. The repartee of Bachchan, Boman Irani and Rajpal Yadav ensures 'laughs aplenty'.
notes: URL not cited in the Wikipedia article; found by Rediff's date pattern.

title: Bunty Aur Babli (2005) review
author: Jaspreet Pandohar
claims: The film teams Bachchan with his son Abhishek. 'Bachchan Sr plays Police Commissioner Dashrath Singh, a sarcastic cop hot on the trail of elusive con artists Bunty (Abhishek Bachchan) and Babli (Rani Mukerji).'

title: Paheli is a breathtaking dream
author: Raja Sen
claims: On the way to the king, the villagers are 'stopped by an eccentric old shepherd, who solves the day with superb, obvious efficiency'. 'Amitabh Bachchan, kajal-eyed and wonderfully mad, is startlingly fantastic in this cameo.'

title: Sarkar is just Godfather, dumbed-down
author: Raja Sen
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan is Sarkar, the Goodfather', 'a mafiosi leader with a strong NGO streak' who 'sits and listens to unjust tales, sending out a righteous army of goons'; his resemblance to Bal Thackeray is 'entirely superficial'. 'Amitabh is incredibly restrained, his character bereft of soliloquy and bluster', and 'given surprisingly little room to perform'. 'Supriya Pathak is perfect as Amitabh's submissive wife.' The film is 'Coppola by numbers'.

title: Sarkar review
author: William Thomas
claims: A 'violent family saga, loosely inspired by The Godfather'. 'Aging Sarkar (or Don) Subhash Nagare (Amitabh Bachchan in a powerhouse performance) is head of the Nagare family working outside the system due to exclusion by social prejudice.'
notes: The page's datePublished is a placeholder (2000-01-01), so no date is entered.

title: AB shines, Viruddh doesn't
author: Savera Someshwar
claims: Bachchan is 'both the star and the soul' of the film. The first half draws the viewer into 'the comfortably warm world of Vidyadhar (Amitabh) and Sumitra Patwardhan (charmingly played by Sharmila Tagore)': 'Their banter, their daily routine underline a bond built over the years. They really look like a couple who, having faced the vicissitudes of life, are now in complete harmony with each other.' They welcome their son's British girlfriend at once; Amar's death is 'a huge blow to his parents', and the second half turns melodramatic.

title: Viruddh review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Viruddh is 'about an aged couple fighting tooth and nail to prove that their slain kid was not a drug peddler', and it 'follows a similar path' to Baghban 'as far as the compatibility of the couple is concerned'. 'The sequences between Amitabh and Sharmila are interesting and so identifiable, you don't really mind the slow pacing of the narrative.'
notes: Rating 3/5 from the page title.

title: Just another love story
author: Sukanya Verma
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan as Jai's pampering Pa and Revathy as his traditionalist Mom complete the family portrait.' In the song 'Mere Munna', 'Big B is liveliness personified'. 'His portrayal of an affectionate father is lined with warmth and spirit.'

title: Amrithdhare: A must watch!
author: Lata Jha
claims: 'Three days of meaningful living is worth many lifetimes of meaningless existence' is 'the message put forward by Amitabh Bachchan in his flash appearance towards the end' of this Kannada marital drama about Puru and Amritha.

title: Amitabh rocks in Ek Ajnabee
author: Vipin Vijayan
claims: Based on Man on Fire, the film 'reinvents Vijay Dinanath Chauhan'. Bachchan plays retired Indian Army Colonel Suryaveer Singh, called to Bangkok by Shekhar to guard eight-year-old Anamika, only daughter of a millionaire couple. During an engagement with terrorists in Kashmir he accidentally shot dead two children, one reason for his heavy drinking. Anamika 'breathes in life into the dead soul of Suryaveer'; after she is kidnapped he 'swears to bring the culprits to book'.

title: Ek Ajnabee review
author: Manish Gajjar
claims: Suryaveer was chosen because Anamika's mother wanted a bodyguard who would also be a friend to her daughter. The girl brings out 'the emotions which have been suppressed by Suryaveer all these years'; when all plans for her release fail, he takes matters into his own hands.
notes: Published December 2005 per the URL path; the page gives no exact date.

title: Don't visit this Family
author: Raja Sen
claims: Bachchan plays Sushant Singh's father, 'a nefarious Dubai-based baddie'. When a misguided bullet hits do-gooder Shekhar (Akshay Kumar), Bachchan kills him to leave no witnesses and drives away. 'Amitabh inexplicably keeps licking his chops'; the stars 'just went through the motions after pocketing fat paychecks'.
notes: Rediff names the character Biren Sahi and places him in Dubai; Wikipedia and India Today say Bangkok.

title: Movie review: 'Family: Ties of Blood' starring Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar
claims: 'Bachchan, as a mafia don who lives in Bangkok, smokes a cigar, wears nifty pinstripes, and looks irritated to be playing the bad guy in a poorly written role.' 'Bachchan's Missing-in-Action performance does nothing either for his oeuvre or for his admirers.'
notes: Text from the page's JSON-LD articleBody; no byline in the extract.

title: Darna Zaroori Hai review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Story 2 (Bachchan and Ritesh Deshmukh, directed by Ram Gopal Varma): 'An aged professor [Bachchan] believes there's someone in his house'; his student advises him to seek psychiatric help, and 'the invisible man finally appears in the mirror'. 'Technically, this isn't a scary story; it has more of shock-value.'
notes: Rating 1.5/5 from the page title.

title: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan's philandering lifestyle provides ample moments of laughter and of course, eye-candy, what with some gorgeous firang babes jumping out of the closet.' He hosts a dinner on Kirron Kher's birthday. The relationship 'between the parent and child [the Bachchans] is delicately handled'. 'Amitabh Bachchan is in superb form.'

title: Review: KANK is an exhausting film
author: Raja Sen
claims: Bachchan plays Abhishek's 'flamboyant dad Sam (sexy Sam, the background score keeps reminding us)', 'a widower who dresses like Snoop Doggy Dogg and cavorts appropriately with blondes'; 'it's fabulous to see Bachchan relish this campy role'. The most compelling character in the film is 'a dad who dresses rather bizarrely'.
notes: URL not cited in the Wikipedia article; found by Rediff's date pattern. Wikipedia quotes Raja Sen's criticism of the script.

title: Akshay Kumar gets a Bhojpuri makeover. Amitabh Bachchan & Dharmendra did it first
author: Harsh Tiwari
claims: Bachchan appeared in the Bhojpuri film Ganga (2006) and its sequel Gangotri (2007). Ganga 'revolves around a young woman in love with Shankar'; 'Thakur Vijay Singh, portrayed by Amitabh Bachchan, uses his influence in the village to arrange her marriage with his son Ranjit, setting the stage for a conflict rooted in power, class, and rural politics'. Hema Malini and Nagma 'also played pivotal roles'. The film was produced by Bachchan's make-up artist Deepak Sawant.
notes: Found by web search; a retrospective feature, not a contemporary review.

title: Big B, Rani excel in Baabul
author: Sudarshana Dwivedi; Sukanya Verma
claims: A two-critic conversation. Verma found it 'easier to identify with Amitabh Bachchan's dilemma'; the rain-drenched scene in which Rani Mukerji's Millie cries 'makes Amitabh alive to her needs and desires', and Bachchan's 'heart-to-heart conversation with his dead son looking at the stars' is a highlight. Dwivedi: 'The chemistry between Amitabh and Salman was excellent throughout. In fact, the relationship between AB and Hema Malini was not as spontaneous in Baabul as it was in Baghban.' Om Puri plays 'Big B's supremely orthodox elder brother'.

title: Eklavya is undeniably impressive
author: Raja Sen
claims: Bachchan narrates the opening credits, explaining the Mahabharata legend of Eklavya. The dying queen (Sharmila Tagore) is tended by the king, who recites Shakespeare's 18th sonnet to her. 'This is an out-and-out Amitabh Bachchan film. Eklavya is conflicted and determined, forceful yet fragile, and — using his eyes to masterful effect — Amitabh hands in a stunning performance.' Jimmy Shergill is 'pitted against Amitabh in the film's finest scene'.

title: Eklavya – The Royal Guard review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'The ghungroo sequence — a blindfolded Bachchan separating the ghungroo from the pigeon — is awe-inspiring'; the film is 'an almost flawless product'.
notes: Rating 4/5 from the page.

title: Nishabd is a powerful film
author: Raja Sen
claims: Varma extracts 'a phenomenal performance from The Megastar'. Standing on a precipice, Bachchan narrates 'the story of a girl that drove him to thoughts of suicide'. 'Amitabh plays Vijay, an introverted, no-nonsense photographer who lives in the heart of a massive tea estate with his wife Amrita (Revathy).' The first half focuses on 'the inevitable spark, the undeniable chemistry, between this perfectly cast odd-couple'; the performance is 'a reinvention so masterful that you can't help but marvel'.

title: Amitabh rocks Cheeni Kum
author: Raja Sen
claims: 'A deftly made May-December love story.' Buddhadeb Gupta (Bachchan), a London restaurateur and 'preachy perfectionist', lays sarcasm on Nina Verma (Tabu) when she sends back a dish, and is then compelled to apologise; 'He's 64, she's 34'. Nina 'lends the pair contrast, gives it chemistry, makes the film work'; 'the repartee between the lead pair is tight'.

title: Shootout at Lokhandwala review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan is not in his element, expect [sic] for the final sequence in the courtroom.'
notes: Rating 3/5 from the page.

title: Jhoom Barabar Jhoom review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan adds to star-value.'
notes: Rating 1.5/5 from the page.

title: Ram Gopal Varma ki.. Aargh!
author: Raja Sen
claims: Casting Bachchan as the villain occasionally elevates the film to 'a Big-B-movie'. His Babban Singh is 'a uniquely twisted individual, with one-brown-one-green eyes', limping in combat boots and a military jacket; 'Bachchan gamely gets into the character'. Babban is 'so over-written it hurts'; 'Amitabh conjures up some great moments, but he was a better villain in Aks'.

title: Review: The Last Lear
author: Sukanya Verma
claims: Inspired by Utpal Dutt's play Aajker Shahjahan. Bachchan plays Harish Mishra aka Harry, 'a theatre actor hailing from the Shakespearean school of thought', and 'essays this startling personality with awe-inspiring ardor'; 'The Last Lear is only about Harry, how he is persuaded to act in a film and his concealed regrets'. Shefali Shah plays 'his live-in companion'. 'This is Bachchan's masterpiece.'

title: The Last Lear is the most god-awful film I have ever seen in any genre, anywhere in the world
author: Nirpal Dhaliwal
claims: Bachchan plays 'a cranky ageing thespian, Harish Mishra, who is lured out of retirement in Calcutta for his first movie role by a hip young director'; his performance 'is so atrocious that I almost puked with laughter at it'.
notes: A polemical blog column rather than a formal review.

title: Bachchans' Bhojpuri outing
author: Girish Rao
claims: The music of the Bhojpuri film Gangotri, 'starring Amitabh Bachchan and Bhojpuri superstar Manoj Tiwari', was launched after the film's release; Bachchan was on stage for five minutes. The film was produced by his make-up man Deepak Sawant.

title: Amitabh Bachchan, Mithun to star in Gangotri
claims: After a hit with Ganga, producer Deepak Sawant, Bachchan's make-up man, planned Gangotri, the first Bhojpuri sequel. 'In the climax of Ganga, Bachchan is shown serving a prison term. In Gangotri, the film will continue with Bachchan's release. Hema Malini will be cast opposite Bachchan.'
notes: A pre-production report; Mithun Chakraborty does not appear in Wikipedia's cast list for the released film.

title: Bhoothnath review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'A simple story, well told.' 'The story rests on two shoulders — the experienced [Bachchan] and the raw talent [Aman Siddiqui] — and both shoulder the responsibility beautifully.'
notes: Rating 4/5 from the page.

title: Review: Sarkar Raj
author: Raja Sen
claims: Calls the film 'a well-lit and overdone follow-up to an overrated original'. Sarkar (Bachchan) wants the villages protected while Shankar looks 'towards the long run', 'and so begins a conflict'.

title: Sarkar Raj
author: Lisa Tsering (The Associated Press)
claims: 'Sixty-five-year-old Amitabh Bachchan, India's vibrant and virile living legend, is riveting in nearly every film he does.'
notes: Only this sentence matched.

title: God Tussi Great Ho review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Arun rages against God, who 'later appears in human form'; the film 'does appeal, but in bits and spurts'.
notes: Rating 2/5 from the page.

title: Delhi-6 review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'The sequence in the end, when Amitabh and Abhishek have a conversation, looks weird. Amitabh Bachchan's presence in the penultimate minutes fails to evoke any reaction.'
notes: Rating 1.5/5 from the page.

title: Aladin review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: The genie Genius (Bachchan) is 'desperate to grant him three wishes and seek the end of his contract with the Magic Lamp' and carries 'the dark secret about Aladin's past'. The track 'when Amitabh loses his powers and becomes an ordinary mortal, looks gimmicky'; 'Amitabh Bachchan is over the top this time'.
notes: Rating 1/5 from the page.

title: Aladin: Save it, Genie!
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan is in fine form, delivering kicks and punchlines with the agility of someone half his age.' Bachchan sings 'You're the one' while Riteish Deshmukh lip-syncs; the film spends 'far too much time on the romance'.
notes: Text from the page's JSON-LD articleBody; no byline in the extract.

title: Paa review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Balki 'transforms the legendary actor into Auro, replaces the rich baritone with the voice of an adolescent'; '10 minutes into the film and you forget you're watching Amitabh Bachchan'. Auro is 'an intelligent, witty 13-year-old boy with an extremely rare genetic defect that causes accelerated ageing'; the climax, when Auro reveals his father's first mistake, is singled out.
notes: Rating 4/5 from the page.

title: Paa — Film Review
author: Frank Lovece (The Associated Press)
claims: The pairing of Amitabh Bachchan and his son Abhishek in 'the tear-stained soaper Paa' seems designed 'to evoke the frisson of Henry and Jane Fonda together in On Golden Pond'.
notes: Only this sentence matched.

title: Rann review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Vijay Harshvardhan Malik (Bachchan) is the founder of the news channel India 24/7; the corrupt politician Mohan Pandey uses Vijay's son-in-law to exploit the channel. 'Amitabh Bachchan is spectacular yet again, especially towards the finale.'
notes: Rating 3.5/5 from the page.

title: Review: Teen Patti is just one big bluff
author: Preeti Arora
claims: Venkat Subramanium (Bachchan) is 'an unsuccessful Maths professor whose superiors claim his research projects have no practical applications'; the persona follows The Last Lear. 'Bachchan does his best but he's tied down with a clichéd script.' His scenes with Ben Kingsley offer 'the sheer pleasure of watching two legends share screen space'.

title: Teen Patti review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: The reclusive genius Venkat has cracked a theory of probability; uninterested in money, 'he eventually succumbs to Shantanu's charismatic persuasion', and the experiment 'soon descends into a game neither of them can control'. Bachchan narrates his side of the story in flashbacks to Ben Kingsley.
notes: Rating 2.5/5 from the page.

title: Review: Big B, Mohanlal shine in Kandahar
claims: 'The highlight of the film is the presence of legendary actor Amitabh Bachchan, for the first time in Malayalam cinema. Amitabh Bachchan has done his part quite elegantly.' Soorya is a hot-blooded youth and 'his father has all his hopes pinned on him'.
notes: Wayback Machine copy; no byline found.

title: Review: Bbuddah Hoga Tera Baap is uber cool
author: Raja Sen
claims: 'Not a particularly well-crafted film but none of that matters as Amitabh Bachchan makes it work.' Bachchan plays 'a retired gangster freshly back in Mumbai' whose character 'despises being called old'; the film is 'a greatest-hits medley: a fight here, a wink there, a little bit of storytelling in that voice, and even the twist'.
notes: Wikipedia reports a 4/5 rating.

title: Aarakshan review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Prabhakar Anand (Bachchan) is 'the idealistic principal of a college that he has single-handedly turned into the state's best'. His conflict with Manoj Bajpayee's character 'is well presented'. 'The Principal's role is tailor-made for Amitabh Bachchan.'
notes: Rating 4/5 from the page.

title: Review: Aarakshan is disappointing
author: Aseem Chhabra
claims: After the interval the film becomes 'an argument against the expensive private tutoring schools', with good 'represented by Amitabh Bachchan's character Prabhakar Anand' and evil by Manoj Bajpayee's Mithilesh Singh. Anand is 'an idealist principal (so much like his other bearded principal performance in Mohabattein)' of a top private college in Bhopal who 'cares for his students'.

title: Department review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan is remarkably credible.'
notes: Rating 2/5 from the page; only this sentence matched.

title: Web search: Yaar Meri Zindagi (2008)
claims: Search summary: Bachchan plays Dr Ajay Singh, 'a compassionate physician dedicated to serving the poor', and Shatrughan Sinha plays Thakur Vikram Singh, 'a powerful landlord'; 'the narrative centers on the childhood friendship between the two protagonists, which deteriorates into rivalry due to ego clashes and personal ambitions'. The film had a limited release of 20 prints in Maharashtra.
notes: IMDb returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches. The summary's wording appears to come from Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, so it is used only for the role outline. It dates the start of shooting to 1971; Wikipedia says 1976.

title: Satyagraha review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'SATYAGRAHA is embellished with qualitative performances, with each actor grabbing eyeballs.' 'Amitabh is incomparable and unmatched yet again, delivering a performance that's easily one amongst his finest in the recent times.' Notes that Bachchan's and Ajay Devgn's characters 'bear striking correlation to real-life characters' and identifies Bachchan's as 'a man who is a firm believer of Gandhian principles'.
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: 'Bhoothnath Returns' review: Amitabh Bachchan gets much more to do this time
author: Shubhra Gupta
claims: 'Finally it was neither funny nor serious enough: neither fully ghostly nor ghastly, but somewhere in between.' Describes Bhoothnath as 'one depressed ghost' humiliated at failing to scare children, and says the political turn makes the film 'one of the sharpest Bollywood critiques of the political system in the country'. Confirms the director as Nitesh Tiwari and Akhrot as Bhoothnath's constant companion.
notes: Recovered through the JSON-LD articleBody; the date comes from the page's article:published_time.

title: Shamitabh review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Summarises the premise: the mute star Daanish is voiced by 'the drunkard Amitabh Sinha (Amitabh Bachchan)' under a contract requiring his silence about the arrangement, and Daanish renames himself Shamitabh. 'As far as the performances are concerned, there are absolutely no points in guessing as to who is the captain of this ship... it's the actor par excellence Amitabh Bachchan.' Notes Balki had earlier directed Bachchan in Cheeni Kum and Paa.
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: Piku review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Describes Piku's world as revolving around her office, her colleague Sayyed Afroze and 'her ever-so-doting father Bhaskhor Banerjee (Amitabh Bachchan)', whose constipation dominates her day. 'This being an author backed role, no prizes for guessing as to it is Deepika Padukone who leads the show from all the fronts. To stand up to the stalwarts like Amitabh Bachchan and Irrfan Khan is no mean achievement.' Notes Bachchan plays against 'his ever-so-towering persona'.
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: Wazir review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Rated 2.5/5. Calls Wazir the only film besides Shatranj Ke Khilari to make chess its central theme. Describes the meeting: as Danish Ali is about to kill himself, 'there enters a chess champion named Panditji aka Omkar Nath Dhar (Amitabh Bachchan) in his life', who teaches him the similarities between the game of life and the game of chess; the two become close over drinks and chess, and Panditji reveals his daughter was murdered by the politician Yazaad Qureshi.
notes: Used in place of the cited Firstpost review, which returned only a 572-byte shell to both curl and the fetcher.

title: Review: TE3N is a weak remake
author: Raja Sen
claims: 'Bachchan is the ideal choice for the part of an inconsolable grandfather, doggedly desperate to find out about a long-ago kidnapping that led to his granddaughter's death. The actor shuffles through both bewilderment and clarity, everything a struggle for his John Biswas, from starting a scooter to remembering the name of the soup he's ma[de].' Opens by noting the film's Gol Maal homage set at a police station.
notes: Recovered through the JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Pink review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Rated 4/5. Introduces 'retired advocate Deepak Sehgal (Amitabh Bachchan)', who volunteers to fight the three women's case 'despite having given up his law practice'. 'PINK is embellished with bravura performances and it is undoubtedly and undisputedly the towering Amitabh Bachchan who steals the show.' Also states that 'the film does not explain certain elements very clearly like the relationship between Amitabh Bachchan with an ailing lady named Sarah'.
notes: The last claim is the basis for creating no Romances row for Deepak and Sara Sehgal.

title: Sarkar 3 review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Rated 2/5: 'Sarkar 3 comes across as an old wine in a new bottle and offers nothing new to the audience.' Describes the film as 'a political thriller with strong undercurrents of strength, might, betrayal, power games and relationships', opening with Subhash Nagre's motivational speech to his followers and building when he refuses to partner on a ₹200 crore Dharavi project, then deviating with the entry of his grandson Shivaji 'Cheeku' Nagre.
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: 102 Not Out review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: '102 NOT OUT is an unusual story of a father and a son. Dattatraya Vakharia (Amitabh Bachchan) is a healthy old man at the ripe age of 102. His son Babulal (Rishi Kapoor) meanwhile is around 75 and has lost interest in life.' Dattatraya cannot tolerate Babulal's negativity about old age and death and decides 'to become the first father ever to admit his son in an old-age home', then sets conditions Babulal must fulfil to stay; as they proceed Dattatraya 'becomes more and more excited and child-like'. Compares the premise to Balki's Cheeni Kum.
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: Thugs Of Hindostan review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'The Aamir Khan starrer Thugs of Hindostan has some engrossing moments in the first half, that's about it.' Confirms the plot: 'The king's guardian, Khudabaksh [Amitabh Bachchan], escapes with the king's daughter Zafira'; eleven years on they are considered thugs, and Clive summons Firangi Mallah to trace Khudabaksh, who enrols in his army. 'Amitabh Bachchan delivers a powerful performance and towers above all.' 'Aamir plays to the gallery, but is letdown by the writing.'
notes: Notes the first pairing of Bachchan and Aamir Khan. No publication date on the page.
