title: Gulabo Sitabo review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan and Ayushmann Khurrana starrer GULABO SITABO is a decent entertainer despite the lack of humour and an average script.' Establishes the relationship: 'Mirza Chunnan Nawab (Amitabh Bachchan), 78, is married to Fatima Begum (Farrukh Jafar), who is nearly 17 years older to him'; Begum owns the century-old Fatima Mahal in Lucknow and, being old 'and also a bit delusional', leaves Mirza to take care of the haveli. Baankey Rastogi's family have been tenants 'since ages' paying merely ₹30 monthly rent, which Mirza wants raised so he can drive them out. Notes the film premiered on a digital platform.
notes: Supports the age gap, the marriage's property basis and the Mirza-Baankey feud used in PAIR-095. No publication date on the page.

title: Chehre review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'CHEHRE is a well-made film which rests on a unique plot and bravura performances.' Sets out the roles: Jagdish Acharya was a retired judge, Paramjeet a defence counsel and 'Lateef was chief prosecutor'; in the game Paramjeet defends while 'Lateef would try to prove that he's guilty'. Lateef stakes his legal reputation on proving Sameer's part in Oswal's murder. 'Amitabh Bachchan's entry is clap worthy.' Recalls his 'No Means No' dialogue in Pink (2016).
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: Jhund review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Rated 4/5. 'JHUND is the story of an unusual football team. Vijay Borade (Amitabh Bachchan) teaches in St John's college', which stands next to a vast slum. He spots slum youths playing football with an abandoned plastic box, goes to the slum the next day and asks them to play for thirty minutes; the children become so attached to the game that 'they agree to play without money'. Vijay proposes a friendly match against the college team, whose coach 'despises these slum children' and pressures his side to score ten goals without conceding.
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: Runway 34 review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Runway 34 boasts of fine performances and a gripping first half', but 'the slow moving and conversation heavy second half limit the Ajay Devgn – Amitabh Bachchan starrer' somewhat. 'Narayan Vedant (Amitabh Bachchan) of AAIB takes up personal interest and decides to drill Vikrant and Tanya.' 'The entry of Narayan Vedant in the second half enhances the excitement.' 'Amitabh Bachchan has a late entry but manages to obviously rock the show.'
notes: Supports recording the role as Co-lead despite the late entry. No publication date on the page.

title: Brahmastra Part One: Shiva review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Describes Anish handing the Brahmāstra fragment to Shiva and Isha and sending them 'to the ashram of Guru (Amitabh Bachchan)' while he tries to stop Junoon. 'Amitabh Bachchan is lovely in a supporting role.'
notes: The basis for recording the role type as Supporting. The slug brahmastra-part-one-shiva returned an empty response; this shorter slug worked. No publication date on the page.

title: Goodbye review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Despite the performances GOODBYE suffers from a weak second half and depressive tone.' Tara learns of her mother Gayatri's death when 'her father Harish (Amitabh Bachchan) calls'; she and Harish 'don't see eye to eye and both clash over the funeral ceremonies', and Harish is upset that Karan and Angad 'don't seem moved by their mother's demise', his behaviour leading to fights in the house. Praises the scene in which the family imagine Gayatri talking to them and 'the animation flashback of Amitabh Bachchan and Neena Gupta', but notes that this and Gayatri's love for the ukulele 'never gets established in the flashback portions'.
notes: The last observation is the basis for creating no Romances row for Harish and Gayatri. No publication date on the page.

title: Uunchai review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'UUNCHAI is a simple, emotional, family film with top notch performances by the lead cast.' 'Amit Shrivastava (Amitabh Bachchan) is a successful author, based in Delhi. He is separated from his wife Abhilasha (Nafisa Ali Sodhi) and the closest people in his life are his three friends – Javed (Boman Irani), Om Sharma (Anupam Kher), and Bhupen (Danny Denzongpa).' Bhupen proposes the Everest Base Camp trek and the others refuse on grounds of age and health; after his death Amit finds that Bhupen had booked the tour for his three friends. Notes this is the director's first film celebrating friendship rather than family.
notes: The source for Amit's separation from Abhilasha, which is stated but not developed in the film. No publication date on the page.

title: Kalki 2898 AD review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'KALKI 2898 AD delivers a unique experience to audiences.' 'All of a sudden, Ashwatthama (Amitabh Bachchan) is awakened and he decides to save Sumati's life at any cost.' 'Amitabh Bachchan shines and how.' Criticises the fight scenes between Bachchan and Prabhas as 'too long and even repetitive'.
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: Director Prayag Raj no more
claims: 'The sudden demise of veteran screenplay writer-director Prayag Raj has left the entire movie industry in shock. Prayag Raj breathed his last on Saturday at his residence in Mumbai.' Reports that celebrities from Amitabh Bachchan to Anil Kapoor paid tribute on social media.
notes: Supplemented by a web search reporting that he died on 23 September 2023 aged 88, wrote Amar Akbar Anthony, Naseeb, Suhaag, Coolie and Mard, had more than 100 films to his credit as writer and a few as lyricist, and also directed. He has no Wikipedia article: a fetch of 'Prayag Raj' resolves to the city Prayagraj, and that page was discarded.

title: 'Mr Natwarlal', 'Yaarana' director Rakesh Kumar dies
publisher: ThePrint / The Tribune / The Week (PTI report)
claims: Rakesh Kumar, the director of Khoon Pasina (1977), Mr. Natwarlal (1979), Do Aur Do Paanch (1980) and Yaarana (1981) with Amitabh Bachchan, died on 10 November 2022 aged 81 after a long battle with cancer. He worked as an assistant director on Prakash Mehra's Zanjeer (1973) before making his directorial debut with Khoon Pasina in 1977; his other credits include Commander, Kaun Jeeta Kaun Haara and Suryavanshi. Bachchan said Kumar left an imprint that is 'hard to remove or forget', praising 'his sense of screenplay and direction, writing and execution on the spur of the moment and the fun times on location'.
notes: No Wikipedia article exists under 'Rakesh Kumar', 'Rakesh Kumar (director)' or 'Rakesh Kumar (film director)'. The bare title was deliberately not fetched because it would resolve to an unrelated person.

title: Web search: Deepak Sawant, Amitabh Bachchan's make-up artist and Bhojpuri producer
publisher: Web search (IMDb, NETTV4U, Wikipedia article on Gangotri)
claims: Search summary: Deepak Sawant has worked with Amitabh Bachchan for more than 35 years as his personal make-up artist. He moved into production and chose Bhojpuri cinema because it required less capital than mainstream Hindi film. He produced three Bhojpuri films — Ganga, Gangotri and Ganga Devi — all starring Bachchan. title: Rajkamal Kalamandir — Wikipedia
claims: Rajkamal Kalamandir was a film production company and studio in Mumbai, established by V. title: Sagar Sarhadi — Wikipedia
claims: Sagar Sarhadi, born Ganga Sagar Talwar (11 May 1933 – 22 March 2021), Indian short-story writer, playwright, and film writer, director and producer, born in Baffa, Mansehra district, in present-day Pakistan, son of Than Singh Talwar and Prem Dai and uncle of Ramesh Talwar. He began writing Urdu short stories and plays before entering film, becoming known with Yash Chopra's Kabhi Kabhi (1976), starring Amitabh Bachchan and Raakhee, for which he wrote screenplay and dialogue. He went on to write Noorie (1979), Silsila (1981), Chandni (1989), Faasle and Rang (1993), and directed Bazaar (1982). He received a Lifetime Achievement Award at the International Cultural Artifact Film Festival. Used for the writer entry.
notes: Downloaded as raw wikitext. The digest script copied the birth date into the death field; both dates here come from the lead prose. Its filmography confirms both credits counted here, listing Kabhi Kabhi as screenplay and dialogue and Silsila as screenplay.

title: Sajid-Farhad — Wikipedia
claims: Sajid-Farhad is an Indian film director and writer duo consisting of the brothers Sajid Samji and Farhad Samji, born into an Aga Khani (Khoja) Nizari Ismaili family. They began as lyricists, brought in by David Dhawan for Hum Kisise Kum Nahin (2002), and first succeeded with the song 'M Bole Toh' from Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. Ram Gopal Varma then hired them for Shiva (2006) and Aag (2007), after which they wrote dialogue for Rohit Shetty's Sunday and Golmaal Returns (2008) and went on to Ready, Singham, Housefull 2, Bol Bachchan, Chashme Baddoor, Himmatwala and Chennai Express. Five of the films they wrote entered the 100-crore club. They began directing with Entertainment (2014), followed by Housefull 3 (2016). Used for the writer entry.

title: Salim Khan — Wikipedia
claims: Salim Abdul Rashid Khan, born 24 November 1935 in Indore, Indian screenwriter, actor and film producer, best known as one half of the screenwriting duo Salim–Javed with Javed Akhtar, among the first Indian screenwriters to achieve star status. Within the partnership Salim Khan primarily developed stories and characters while Akhtar focused on dialogue and screenplay. The pair transformed the Hindi narrative formula, pioneered the blockbuster and masala forms, and were instrumental in creating the 'angry young man' archetype that defined Amitabh Bachchan's career. The article states that Salim Khan was instrumental in launching Bachchan, who was a struggling actor before Salim–Javed insisted on casting him in lead roles, and that Khan personally introduced Bachchan to directors including Prakash Mehra and Manmohan Desai. Their credits include Zanjeer (1973), Majboor (1974), Sholay (1975), Deewaar (1975), Immaan Dharam (1977), Trishul and Don (1978). Used for the writer entry.
notes: Downloaded as raw wikitext. Its Filmfare table lists 1974 Zanjeer (Best Screenplay, Best Story), 1976 Deewaar (Best Dialogue, Screenplay, Story) and 1983 Shakti (Best Screenplay) but leaves every Outcome cell blank, so no win is asserted from it. Important for reading the row: the workbook counts Salim–Javed as a separate team entry, so only his two solo credits, Toofan and Akayla, fall under this person id.

title: Sanchit Balhara and Ankit Balhara — Wikipedia
claims: Sanchit Balhara and Ankit Balhara are an Indian film score composer duo, brothers born in Sonipat, Haryana, to the Haryanvi singer, actor and filmmaker Bhal Singh Balhara and the national-level athlete Mukta Chaudhary. Their scores include Padmaavat (2018), Kalank and War (2019), Panga and Khaali Peeli (2020), Radhe (2021), Gangubai Kathiawadi and Radhe Shyam (2022). Ankit is married to the field hockey player Savita Punia. Used for the background-score-composer entry.

Murali Manohar, she produced Indian, American and British films including Indian Summer (1987), Blood Stone (1988), Jeans (Tamil, 1998), Jodi (1999), Minnale (2001), Jungle Boy (2001), Majnu (2002), Tropical Heat (2002), Arasatchi (2003), Backwaters (2004), Ramji Londonwaley (2005), Telling Lies (2005), Inferno (2006), Provoked (2006), Sajni (Kannada, 2007), Dhaam Dhoom (2008), Chikku Bukku (2010), Mirattal (2012) and Kochadaiiyaan (2014). In 2001 she launched South for You, a south Indian Tamil channel on the Sky network in Britain, running it until she sold it in 2011, after which UTV took it over.

His lyric credits run from Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi (2003) through Parineeta, Sehar, Lage Raho Munna Bhai, Laaga Chunari Mein Daag and Khoya Khoya Chand; he appeared as Sansad ji in Panchayat 3 and as Mansoor Khan Sahab in Qala, to whose soundtrack he also contributed.

The two National Film Award wins are asserted in the lead prose, not read off the awards table, whose Result cells are blank.

title: T-Series (company)

It is the largest music label in India with up to a 35 per cent share of the Indian music market, and as of August 2026 owns the most-viewed and second most-subscribed YouTube channel, with over 353 billion views and 314 million subscribers. Though best known as a music label, T-Series has produced more than 100 films and is a leading Hindi film production company. Its chairman and managing director is Bhushan Kumar, with Krishan Kumar and president Neeraj Kalyan among its key people.

title: Meet producers Tito and Tony, who first brought Amitabh Bachchan, Rekha together on screen; defied Jaya Bachchan
claims: The producer brothers credited simply as Tito and Tony were born Kushaljeet Singh Juneja and Ramanjit Singh Juneja in Punjab, sons of a liquor supplier to Army canteen stores and Indian Army troops who owned liquor warehouses in Nagaland. They began by producing Assamese films in Guwahati, moved to Bombay and worked at Roop Tara Studios, and in the 1970s launched their own banner, Navjeevan Films. Their debut production was Do Anjaane (1976), a commercial success that first paired Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha on screen; they followed it with Mr. Natwarlal (1979), a blockbuster made despite distributor skepticism, and Ram Balram (1980), 'a smashing hit'. Later productions — Ek Aur Sikander, Teri Kasam, Johny I Love You, Aasman, Babu, Abhimanyu, Ithihas, Ram Tera Desh, Insaniyat and Out of Control — 'didn't taste much success', and the brothers gradually distanced themselves from films as Bachchan's popularity waned in the late 1980s and 1990s.
notes: The article gives no birth or death dates. It documents two roster artifacts. First, the same producer appears in the Films sheet under two name strings — 'Tito' on Do Anjaane and Ram Balram, and 'Tito Juneja' on Insaniyat (FILM-127) — so the frozen roster counts two films for PERSON-234 when the workbook's own data supports three; this is the S. D. Burman / Sachin Dev Burman split of batch 5 in a new form. Second, the article credits the brothers with Mr. Natwarlal (1979), which the workbook (FILM-065) attributes to 'Tony Glaad' under the banner spelling 'Navjeevan Productions', so a fourth Bachchan film is theirs on this source's account. His brother Tony is in the roster separately as PERSON-284, Ramanjit 'Tony' Juneja, credited as director of Insaniyat; the banner Navjeevan Films is PERSON-188.

title: Vaishal Shah
claims: Vaishal Shah, born 10 November 1984 in Ahmedabad and active since 2015, is an Indian film producer working in Gujarati, Marathi and Hindi cinema. His productions include Chhello Divas (2015), Karsandas Pay & Use (2017), Shu Thayu? (2018), Fakt Mahilao Maate (2022), 3 Ekka (2023), Fakt Purusho Maate (2024) and Chaniya Toli (2025). He was the first producer to bring the actors Malhar Thakar, Yash Soni and Mitra Gadhavi together, in Chhello Divas, and again in Shu Thayu? and 3 Ekka, both of which rank among the ten highest-grossing Gujarati films. In 2021 he worked with the producer Anand Pandit as co-producer of the Hindi film Chehre, starring Amitabh Bachchan and Emraan Hashmi; the two went on to produce Fakt Mahilao Maate (2022), Fakt Purusho Maate (2024), Chaniya Toli (2025) and Asambhauuu (2026) together.
notes: The article states he produces films that entertain while carrying a social message. It documents a third Bachchan film, Chehre (2021), that the frozen roster does not count for him: the Chehre wikitext links his name but the workbook's producer field for that film credits Anand Pandit's banner, so his roster count of two understates the working relationship.

title: Vanraj Bhatia
claims: Vanraj Bhatia (31 May 1927 – 7 May 2021), born and died in Bombay, was an Indian composer best known for his work in Indian New Wave cinema and one of the leading composers of Western classical music in India. He won the National Film Award for Best Music Direction for the television film Tamas (1988), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Creative and Experimental Music (1989) and the Padma Shri (2012). His other awards include the Lili Boulanger Memorial Fund (1957), Bengal Film Journalists Association awards for the music of Manthan (1976) and Bhumika (1977), the Sur Singar Samsad Award for best classical score in 1986 and 1987, and the Maharashtra Rajya Puraskar (1990). The article lists his compositions across solo piano, chamber music, vocal music, large ensemble, opera, feature film scores, television scores, documentary scores, theatre music and albums.
notes: The infobox death field repeats the birth date, the known digest bug; dates are from the lead. The article does not mention Bachchan. Both of his credits here are background scores, not songs, which is consistent with a composer whose reputation rests on art cinema and concert music rather than film songs.

title: Viacom18 Studios
claims: Viacom18 Studios, formerly Viacom18 Motion Pictures, was an Indian film production and distribution company based in Mumbai and a subsidiary of JioStar, the joint venture of Reliance Industries, Viacom18 and Disney India. It was one of the first studio-model motion picture and content production businesses in India, covering acquisition, production, syndication, marketing and worldwide distribution of feature films, digital-only films, web series and short films, and from 2011 it distributed Paramount Pictures films in India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, beginning with Transformers: Dark of the Moon. Its chief operating officer was Ajit Andhare. Following the merger of Viacom18 and Disney Star, the company was merged into Star Studios to form Star Studio18.
notes: The roster carries the studio under its former name, Viacom18 Motion Pictures, which is what both film wikitexts use; the Boss wikitext pipes [[Viacom18 Studios|Viacom18 Motion Pictures]]. The article does not mention Bachchan. The company no longer exists under either name.

title: Vijay Raghav Rao
claims: Pandit Vijay Raghav Rao, born Vijaya Raghava Rao in Chennai on 3 November 1925 and died 30 November 2011, was an Indian flautist, composer, choreographer, musicologist, poet and fiction writer. He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1970 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in the Creative and Experimental Music category in 1982, the academy's highest honour for a performing artist. His students included G. S. Sachdev, Ronu Majumdar and Deepak Ram.
notes: A short article with no short description and only a Personal life section; the infobox death field repeats the birth date, the known digest bug, so dates are from the lead. It does not mention either of the films counted here, nor Bachchan. The credits rest on the film articles themselves: the Bhuvan Shome and Cinema Cinema wikitexts both give him as composer.

title: Viju Shah
claims: Vijay Shah, known as Viju Shah, born 5 June 1959 and active since 1989, is an Indian composer in the Hindi film industry and the son of Kalyanji Virji Shah, one half of the composer duo Kalyanji–Anandji. He has composed soundtracks for more than 20 Hindi films, among them Tridev (1989), Vishwatma (1992), Mohra (1994), Gupt: The Hidden Truth (1997) and Bade Miyan Chote Miyan (1998), and won the Filmfare Award for Best Background Score in 1998 for Gupt. The article notes that he composed the soundtrack for the romantic drama Tere Mere Sapne (1996), produced by Amitabh Bachchan's ABCL.
notes: His father's duo, Kalyanji–Anandji, is PERSON-005 in this roster with a large Bachchan filmography of its own, so the two credits counted here are the second generation of an established Bachchan collaboration. The article explicitly ties Tere Mere Sapne to ABCL, Bachchan's company, which is PERSON-015.

title: Vipul Shah
claims: Vipul Amrutlal Shah is an Indian film producer and director of Hindi films who began in Gujarati theatre, directing a number of well-received Gujarati plays, and made his film debut with the Gujarati film Dariya Chhoru in the late 1990s with J. D. Majethia in the lead. As of 2010 he had directed six Hindi films, four of them starring Akshay Kumar. His directing credits include Dariya Chhoru (1999), Aankhen (2002) with Amitabh Bachchan, Sushmita Sen, Akshay Kumar, Arjun Rampal and Paresh Rawal, Waqt: The Race Against Time (2005) with Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar, Priyanka Chopra and Shefali Shah, Namastey London (2007), London Dreams (2009) and Action Replayy (2010). He produced and wrote The Kerala Story and is associated with its sequel, The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond.
notes: The article's short description gives his birth year as 1973, which the body does not corroborate. He directed both of his Bachchan films and also produced Waqt, so the roster's combined Director; Writer; Producer function is accurate. His wife, the actress Shefali Shah, appears in both films.

title: Vishal Bhardwaj
claims: Vishal Bhardwaj, born 4 August 1965 in Chandpur, Uttar Pradesh, and active since 1995, is an Indian filmmaker, music composer and playback singer, the recipient of nine National Film Awards and a Filmfare Award. He debuted as a composer on the children's film Abhay (1995) and gained wider recognition with Gulzar's Maachis (1996), for which he won the Filmfare R. D. Burman Award for New Music Talent, then composed for Satya (1998) and Godmother (1999), winning the National Film Award for Best Music Direction for the latter. He made his directorial debut with Makdee (2002) and won acclaim for his Indian adaptations of three Shakespeare tragedies — Maqbool (2003) from Macbeth, Omkara (2006) from Othello and Haider (2014) from Hamlet. He won further National Film Awards for The Blue Umbrella, a Special Jury Award for Omkara, Best Music Direction for Ishqiya and, at the 62nd National Film Awards, Best Music Direction and Best Screenplay for Haider. His films are described as twisted, with grey-shaded characters, frequently adapting short stories and plays — The Blue Umbrella and 7 Khoon Maaf from Ruskin Bond — and drawing on real events, with the Kashmir conflict in Haider, the Mumbai underworld in Maqbool and the 2008 Noida double murder in Talvar. He collaborates frequently with the writer-lyricist Gulzar, whom he calls his father. He is married to the singer Rekha Bhardwaj.
notes: The article does not mention Bachchan. Both credits counted here are composing jobs on other directors' films, not his own directing work, so this is one of the clearest cases in the batch where the collaboration is marginal to the collaborator's real significance.

He then directed Boss (2013), an action comedy starring Akshay Kumar, written by Farhad-Sajid and produced by Ashwin Varde, a remake of the 2010 Malayalam film Pokkiri Raja; Variety and The Hollywood Reporter both reviewed it. His awards table lists an AACTA nomination for Best Asian Film for Thappad (2020) and IIFA nominations for Article 15 in Best Film, Best Director, Best Story and Best Screenplay.

title: Web search: Ashok Gupta and the production history of Yaar Meri Zindagi
publisher: Web search (IMDb, Filmibeat, Rotten Tomatoes, Amazon; Wikipedia article on Yaar Meri Zindagi)
claims: Search summary: Yaar Meri Zindagi is a 2008 Hindi action film directed by Ashok Gupta, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Shatrughan Sinha, Sharada and Sudha Chandran, released on 22 April 2008 with a limited run of about 20 prints in Mumbai and the rest of Maharashtra; its story follows two friends, a Thakur and a doctor, whose egos clash until they turn on each other. The Wikipedia article's production section states that shooting began in 1976 under the director Mukul Dutt, who left the project in 1984 after 'numerous problems and creative differences'; Ashok Gupta then took over as director in 1998 and completed the film within a year, but had further difficulty getting it released. The score is by R. D. Burman, who died in 1994.

Do not confuse him with the editor 'Nipun Ashok Gupta', a different person credited on Aag (2007), Sarkar Raj and Ghoomer, whose name matches on a substring search of the cached wikitext. The 32-year production span, 1976 to 2008, is the longest of any film in this filmography and explains the posthumous R. D. Burman score; Wikipedia files the film under 'Rediscovered Indian films' and '1970s rediscovered films'.

title: Ayan Mukerji
claims: Ayan Deb Mukerji, born 15 August 1983 in Calcutta and active since 2004, is an Indian filmmaker in Hindi cinema and a member of the Mukherjee-Samarth family, known for his collaborations with the actor Ranbir Kapoor under Karan Johar's Dharma Productions. He made his directorial debut with the coming-of-age film Wake Up Sid (2009), which drew strong reviews and box-office returns, and followed it with the romantic comedy-drama Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani (2013) and the fantasy action-adventure Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva (2022), both among the highest-grossing Hindi films. All three earned him Filmfare Best Director nominations, and Wake Up Sid won him the Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director. The article states that he wrote and directed Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva starring Kapoor, Amitabh Bachchan, Alia Bhatt, Mouni Roy and Nagarjuna.
notes: The Filmfare Best Debut Director win is asserted in the lead prose; the awards table's Result cells are blank, so nothing is read off it.

title: B. R. Ishara
claims: Babu Ram Ishara, born Roshan Lal Sharma on 7 September 1934 at Bharwain, Chintpurni, in Una district, Himachal Pradesh, and died in Mumbai on 25 July 2012, was an Indian film director and screenwriter best known for his 1970s films. He made 35 Hindi films between 1964 and 1996, among them Chetana, Log Kya Kahenge, Milap, Man Jaiye, Ghar Ki Laaj, Woh Phir Aayegi and Sautela Bhai. The article records that he worked with a number of newcomers including Danny Denzongpa, Rakesh Pandey, Vijay Arora, Jaya Bhaduri, Amitabh Bachchan, Reena Roy, Shatrughan Sinha, Raj Kiran and Raza Murad. He was married to the actress Rehana Sultan.

title: Bejoy Nambiar
claims: Bejoy Nambiar, born 12 April 1979 in Mumbai, is an Indian film director and screenwriter working in Hindi films, known for his critically acclaimed short films Rahu and Reflections, both starring Mohanlal. He won Sony PIX's Gateway to Hollywood as best director, judged by Ashok Amritraj, Rajat Kapoor and Anurag Basu. He made his feature debut with the thriller Shaitan (2011), followed by the bilingual anthology drama David in Hindi and Tamil, and Taish (2020), released on ZEE5. The article records that he directed Wazir (2016), starring Amitabh Bachchan and Farhan Akhtar, and the short video 'Sachinocalypse' for All India Bakchod. His awards table lists 2012 nominations for Shaitan: Producers Guild Best Screenplay, Screen Awards for Best Director, Most Promising Debut Director and Best Screenplay, and a Stardust Best Director nomination.

title: C. V. Sridhar
claims: Chithamur Vijayaraghavalu Sridhar (22 July 1933 – 20 October 2008), born in Chithamur in the Madras Presidency and died in Chennai, was an Indian screenwriter and film director who directed nearly 60 films in Tamil, Hindi and Telugu between 1959 and 1991. He worked through the banners Venus Pictures and his own Chitralaya. He won a Certificate of Merit for Best Feature Film in Tamil for Kalyana Parisu (1959), the President's Silver Medal for Best Feature Film in Tamil for Nenjil Or Aalayam (1962), the Filmfare Award for Best Story for Nazrana (1961), the Kalaimamani Award and the Tamil Nadu State Arignar Anna Award in 1997, and was nominated for the Filmfare Awards for Best Director and Best Story for Dil Ek Mandir (1963) and for Filmfare Best Tamil Director for Urimai Kural (1975) and Ilamai Oonjal Aadukirathu. He was known as the 'nava-rasa director' for working across registers from the comedy Kaadhalikka Neramillai to the serious Kalai-kovil and Nenjil Or Aalayam, the last of which he remade in Hindi as Dil Ek Mandir; he drew out the comedians T. R. Ramachandran, K. A. Thangavelu and Nagesh and introduced Murthy and Nirmala in Vennira Aadai.
notes: The infobox death field gives 16 August 1933, which is neither his birth date nor his death date; the lead's dates are used. The article does not mention Bachchan. Chitralaya, the banner on Gehri Chaal, is his own company, so director, producer and banner on that film are one person.

title: Chandra Barot
claims: Chandra Barot (1939 – 20 July 2025), born and raised in the Tanganyika Territory and died in Bandra, Mumbai, was an Indian film director in the Hindi film industry, active from 1970 to 2025 and best known for directing Don (1978), which attained cult status and inspired remakes and sequels including the 2006 Shah Rukh Khan version, which caused some controversy. He moved from Tanzania to India and joined the actor-director Manoj Kumar as an assistant director, assisting him on Purab Aur Pachhim (1970), Yaadgaar (1970), Shor (1972) and Roti Kapda Aur Makaan (1974). Before Don was completed, its producer Nariman Irani died: during the shooting of Manoj Kumar's Kranti in November 1977 at Rajkamal Kalamandir Studios in Bombay, a sudden cloudburst brought a wall down on him and he was seriously injured and hospitalised.
notes: The article does not mention Bachchan by name even though Don is its subject. It links two other roster rows: Nariman Irani, Don's producer, and Rajkamal Studios, the sixth studio-field facility identified in batch 5, where the accident that killed Irani happened. Don was Barot's directorial debut and he directed only a handful of films afterwards.

title: Web search: Desh Mukherjee, art director and director of Immaan Dharam
publisher: Web search (IMDb name page, Letterboxd, bachchansir.blogspot.com, brns.com; Wikipedia article on Immaan Dharam)

Immaan Dharam was his directorial debut; the film failed at the box office and he returned to set design, directing only one more film, Aatank (1996), about twenty years later. title: Khwaja Ahmad Abbas
claims: Khwaja Ahmad Abbas (7 June 1914 – 1 June 1987), born in Panipat, Punjab, and died in Bombay, was an Indian film director, screenwriter, novelist and journalist working in Urdu, Hindi and English, active from 1935 to 1987. He won four National Film Awards; internationally his films won the Palme d'Or at Cannes, from three nominations, and the Crystal Globe at Karlovy Vary. He is considered a pioneer of Indian parallel or neo-realist cinema. As a director he made Dharti Ke Lal (1946), about the Bengal famine of 1943, one of Indian cinema's first social-realist films, which opened the Soviet market to Indian films; Pardesi (1957) was nominated at Cannes; Shehar Aur Sapna (1963) won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film; and Saat Hindustani (1969) and Do Boond Pani (1972) both won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration. In 1951 he founded his own production company, Naya Sansar, which produced socially engaged films including Anhonee, Munna, Rahi (1953), Shehar Aur Sapna and Saat Hindustani. As a screenwriter he wrote Naya Sansar (1941), for which he won a BFJA Best Screenplay award in 1942, Awaara (1951), nominated at Cannes, and Jagte Raho (1956), which won the Crystal Globe at Karlovy Vary in 1957 and a Certificate of Merit at the fourth National Film Awards.
notes: The infobox is malformed — the birth_date field contains the birth_place text and the death_date field holds the birth date — so all dates are taken from the lead. title: Raj Khosla
claims: Raj Khosla, born Desraj Khosla on 31 May 1925 in Rahon, Punjab, and died in Bombay on 9 June 1991, was among the leading directors, producers and screenwriters in Hindi cinema from the 1950s to the 1980s, active 1949–1989. He was known for bringing neo-noir and style to Indian cinema and as a 'women's director' who showcased actresses at their best, and he made many successful films with Dev Anand. He began his career under Guru Dutt and directed C.I.D. (1956), Woh Kaun Thi? (1964), Mera Saaya (1966), Mera Gaon Mera Desh (1971), Main Tulsi Tere Aangan Ki (1978), which won the Filmfare Award for Best Film, and Dostana (1980). His early background in classical music ensured that most of his films excelled in music, and he, Guru Dutt and Vijay Anand were inspired by the Alfred Hitchcock school of mystery-suspense thrillers. The article records that after big hits like Main Tulsi Tere Aangan Ki and Dostana (1980) with Amitabh Bachchan, Zeenat Aman and Shatrughan Sinha, Khosla ran into rough weather as his other films began to flop. His awards table lists Filmfare nominations for Best Director for Do Raaste (1971) and Main Tulsi Tere Aangan Ki (1979) and Best Film for the latter.
notes: The infobox repeats the birth date in the death field, the known digest bug; dates are from the lead. Vijay Anand, named in the same sentence about Hitchcock's influence, is PERSON-300 in this batch.

title: Rakesh Roshan

His work includes Khudgarz (1987), Khoon Bhari Maang (1988), Kishen Kanhaiya (1990), Karan Arjun (1995), Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai (2000), Koi... Mil Gaya (2003) and the Krrish series (2006–13). He won the Filmfare Awards for Best Film and Best Director for Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai and Koi... Mil Gaya. He was honoured on 3 December 2006 at the International Film Festival of India in Panaji for his contribution to mainstream cinema, and on 11 December 2006 at the Global Indian Film Awards for his contribution to Indian cinema over 35 years. In 2025 Netflix released a four-part documentary series about him.
notes: The article does not mention Amitabh Bachchan, who narrates Krrish 3 (2013) — the only credit counted here. It carries a dedicated 'Hrithik's career' section, his son being the star of the Krrish films.

title: Web search: Ramanjit 'Tony' Juneja, director of Insaniyat
publisher: Web search (IMDb name and biography pages, Letterboxd, Indian Film History; Wikipedia article on Insaniyat (1994 film))
claims: Search summary: Insaniyat (1994) was directed by Ramanjit 'Tony' Juneja and produced by Tito Juneja under the banner Navjeevan Films. Tony Juneja is the brother of Tito Juneja, the film's producer, and changed his name from Ramanjit Singh Juneja to Tony Juneja for his film work. The film was released on 11 March 1994 with an ensemble cast including Amitabh Bachchan, Sunny Deol, Jaya Prada, Raveena Tandon and Chunky Panday.
notes: This closes the reconciliation opened in batch 6. It confirms independently that PERSON-234 'Tito' and the 'Tito Juneja' credited as producer on Insaniyat (FILM-127) are the same man, Kushaljeet Singh Juneja — so the frozen roster counts two films for him where the workbook's own data supports three, and a DNA feature (SOURCE-814) adds Mr. Natwarlal as a likely fourth. The brothers' banner, Navjeevan Films, is PERSON-188. No Wikipedia article, birth date or death date was located for Tony Juneja.

title: Ravikant Nagaich
claims: Ravikant Nagaich (5 July 1931 – 6 January 1991), born at Atrauli, Aligarh, in the United Provinces and died in Madras, was an Indian director and cinematographer active from 1955 to 1988. He began as a cinematographer in Telugu films, his first being N. T. Rama Rao's Sri Seetha Rama Kalyanam in 1961. With Farz he turned to Hindi films and to direction; this low-budget thriller inspired by James Bond was a surprise hit and helped the careers of its lead pair, Jeetendra and Babita. Dharmendra played Agent 116 Gopal in Keemat (1973), and Jeetendra reprised the Agent 116 role as Gopalkishan Pandey in Raksha (1982) and again in The Gold Medal. He went on to direct 24 more films, the last being Duty (1986). Although he had big-budget hits such as Mere Jeevan Saathi and The Train, his remembered successes are low-budget secret-agent films like Surakksha and Wardat, recalled for their tacky stunts and special effects.
notes: The infobox repeats the birth date in the death field, the known digest bug; dates are from the lead. The article does not mention Bachchan or Pyar Ki Kahani (1971), the film counted here, which is one of the earliest in the filmography.

title: Ribhu Dasgupta
claims: Ribhu Dasgupta, born in Kolkata, is an Indian film and television director. He made his directorial debut with the 2011 film Michael, for which he was nominated at the Shanghai International Film Festival for the Asian New Talent Award for Best Film.
notes: A short article with no birth year and no account of his later work; it does not mention Bachchan or Te3n. The substance of his row comes from the accompanying web search, SOURCE-888.

title: Rituparno Ghosh
claims: Rituparno Ghosh (31 August 1963 – 30 May 2013), born and died in Kolkata, was an Indian film director, actor, writer and lyricist, active 1992–2013. After a degree in economics he began as a creative artist at an advertising agency. He won recognition for his second feature, Unishe April, which won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film, and with his contemporaries Aparna Sen and Goutam Ghose he carried contemporary Bengali cinema to greater heights, winning 19 National Awards in all — the article elsewhere says 12 national and numerous international awards across almost two decades. He was one of the openly homosexual personalities in Indian cinema. He was influenced by Satyajit Ray, was an avid reader of Rabindranath Tagore, whose works are frequently referenced in his films, and made a documentary, Jeevan Smriti, on Tagore's life. He died of a heart attack on 30 May 2013. His National Film Awards include Unishe April (1995), Dahan (1998, Best Screenplay and Best Bengali Film), Asukh (2000), Utsab (2001, Best Direction), Shubho Mahurat (2003) and Chokher Bali (2004). His 2007 film The Last Lear concerned a retired Shakespearean theatre actor, with Amitabh Bachchan in the lead and Preity Zinta and Arjun Rampal in support. The article records that Amitabh Bachchan remembered Ghosh as the only director who had worked with every member of the Bachchan family.
notes: The article contradicts itself on his award count, giving 19 National Awards in one sentence and 12 in another; both figures are recorded rather than reconciled. Its infobox repeats the birth date in the death field, so dates are from the lead. Bachchan's tribute — that Ghosh was the only director to have worked with every member of his family — is the single most substantive statement about the collaboration in this batch.

title: Rohit Shetty
claims: Rohit Shetty, born 14 March 1974 in Mangaluru and active since 1991, is an Indian director, screenwriter, stuntman, producer and television personality in Hindi cinema whose films mix action comedy and masala. His breakthrough was Golmaal (2006) with Ajay Devgn, Tusshar Kapoor and Arshad Warsi, a sleeper hit followed by Golmaal Returns (2008), Golmaal 3 (2010) and Golmaal Again (2017), each among the highest-grossing films of its year. After his debut action thriller Zameen (2003) he returned to action with Singham (2011), also with Devgn, one of the year's highest grossers, which expanded into a Cop Universe including Singham Returns (2014), Simmba (2018) and Sooryavanshi (2021). His other successes include All the Best: Fun Begins (2009), Bol Bachchan (2012) and Chennai Express (2013), the last of which became the highest-grossing Hindi film at the time, surpassing 3 Idiots. The article notes that Bol Bachchan also features Abhishek Bachchan and that both it and Singham crossed the 100 Crore Club domestically. His awards tables list Best Director nominations for Chennai Express at the Filmfare, Producers Guild, BIG Star and Bollywood Hungama awards.
notes: Every Result cell across the awards tables is blank, so no win is asserted from them. The article's many Bachchan mentions refer to Abhishek Bachchan and to the film title Bol Bachchan rather than to Amitabh Bachchan, who appears in that film as himself.

title: S. S. Balan
claims: S. Balasubramanian (28 December 1935 – 19 December 2014), better known as S. S. Balan, born and died in Chennai, was an Indian journalist, filmmaker, political analyst and media executive with a six-decade career in Indian media. He was editor of the Tamil-language magazine Ananda Vikatan and managing director of Gemini Studios from the 1950s, and later served as chairman of the Vikatan Group. The article carries a Filmography section.
notes: Identification confirmed by two independent details rather than by the name alone: Sanjog (1972), the film counted here, was produced by Gemini Studios, of which he was managing director; and the Zanjeer article's remake table credits him as director of Sirithu Vazha Vendum (1974), the Tamil remake of Zanjeer starring M. G. Ramachandran. He therefore directed both a Bachchan film and the Tamil remake of Bachchan's breakthrough film. His article does not mention Bachchan and its infobox repeats the birth date in the death field, so dates are from the lead.

title: Sajid Khan (director)
claims: Sajid Kamran Khan, born 23 November 1970 in Mumbai, is an Indian film director, television presenter, comedian and actor in the Hindi film industry, best known for the Housefull series, Heyy Babyy (2007) and Humshakals (2014). He served as a judge on the reality show Nach Baliye and participated in Bigg Boss 16 in 2022. He is the brother of the choreographer and director Farah Khan. The article carries a section headed 'Allegations of sexual harassment'.
notes: The harassment allegations section is noted but not summarised here. He is the brother of Farah Khan, PERSON-257, written in batch 6 — the only sibling pair in the roster in which both members direct a Bachchan film, though neither directs him in a conventional role: hers is a self-appearance in Om Shanti Om, his a segment of the Darna Zaroori Hai anthology. The article does not mention Bachchan.

title: Sanjay Leela Bhansali
claims: Sanjay Navin Bhansali, born 24 February 1963 in Bombay and known professionally as Sanjay Leela Bhansali — Leela being a matronymic — is an Indian filmmaker and music composer in Hindi cinema, active since 1996 and the recipient of seven National Film Awards and thirteen Filmfare Awards, with a BAFTA nomination. The Government of India honoured him with the Padma Shri in 2015. He is known for his aesthetics and musical vision, particularly in period dramas. He debuted with the romantic musical Khamoshi: The Musical (1996) and found mainstream and critical success with Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999) and Devdas (2002), the latter winning the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment and a BAFTA nomination for Best Film Not in the English Language. The article records that his next film, Black, starring Amitabh Bachchan and Rani Mukerji, broke his own record set by Devdas by taking 11 awards, the highest number ever given to a single film at the Filmfare Awards.
notes: The Filmfare record for Black is the article's own claim and is recorded as such. Black is the film for which Bachchan won the Filmfare Award for Best Actor and which the workbook records as a romance-free film despite its intense teacher–pupil relationship.

title: Web search: Shankar Mukherjee, director of Faraar
publisher: Web search (IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes, Yidio; Wikipedia articles on Faraar (1975 film) and Parayanumvayya Parayathirikkanumvayya)
claims: Search summary: Faraar is a 1975 Hindi crime film produced by Alankar Chitra and directed by Shankar Mukherjee, released on 21 November 1975, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Sharmila Tagore, Sanjeev Kumar, Sulochana, Sajjan, Agha and Bhagwan Dada, with music by Kalyanji–Anandji. It was later remade in Malayalam by Priyadarshan as Parayanumvayya Parayathirikkanumvayya.
notes: No Wikipedia article and no biographical information of any kind located — not a birth year, not a second credit. A bare Wikipedia fetch returned the 1929-byte error page. Everything recorded for him is film-level rather than personal. Faraar is also one of the films whose Wikipedia plot the workbook flagged in phase 2 as reading like an unsourced retelling, so the film article is used with care.

title: Shashi Kapoor
claims: Shashi Kapoor, born Balbir Raj Kapoor on 18 March 1938 in Calcutta and died in Mumbai on 4 December 2017, was an Indian actor and producer in Hindi films, considered one of the greatest actors in the history of Hindi cinema and the recipient of four National Film Awards and two Filmfare Awards. The Government of India honoured him with the Padma Bhushan in 2011 and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2014. Born into the Kapoor family as the youngest son of Prithviraj Kapoor, he began as a child actor in 1948 in his brother Raj Kapoor's first film as director, Aag, and had his first adult role in 1961 in Yash Chopra's Dharmputra, establishing himself in 1965 with Waqt and Jab Jab Phool Khile. The article states that 1975 was another iconic year for him, as he formed a hit pair with Amitabh Bachchan, the two giving Hindi cinema many successful and iconic films: Deewaar, directed by Yash Chopra and written by Salim–Javed, was a critical and commercial blockbuster; Kabhie Kabhie had a massive cast of Waheeda Rehman, Bachchan, Rishi Kapoor, Rakhee and Neetu Singh; they reunited for Desh Mukherjee's Immaan Dharam (1977), which opened big but flopped; for Yash Chopra's Kaala Patthar and Manmohan Desai's Suhaag in 1979; and for Prakash Mehra's Namak Halaal (1982), a blockbuster. The article further records that Shashi Kapoor requested Amitabh Bachchan to star in his ambitious directorial debut Ajooba (1991), and that Bachchan made a notable exception and agreed because of their friendship, even though at the time he was not signing any new films.
notes: The infobox gives a death date of 3 April 1938, which is neither his birth nor his death; the lead's dates are used. This is the most Bachchan-dense article in the whole roster, since the two men made a dozen films together as actors — but the frozen roster counts Kapoor only once, for directing and producing Ajooba, because his acting credits are not a collaborator function this workbook tracks. Desh Mukherjee, named here, is PERSON-255.

title: Sooraj Barjatya
claims: Sooraj R. Barjatya, born 22 February 1964 in Bombay and active since 1989, is an Indian filmmaker in Hindi cinema who has directed and produced some of the most commercially successful Hindi films, with recurring themes of familial ties and values rooted in traditional Indian culture. He is chairman of Rajshri Productions, formed by his late grandfather Tarachand Barjatya in 1947. He began as an assistant director to Mahesh Bhatt and made his directorial debut with Maine Pyar Kiya (1989), a top-grossing romantic drama; his next release, Hum Aapke Hain Koun..! (1994), became the highest-grossing Indian film to that point. He had further success with Hum Saath-Saath Hain (1999), Vivah (2006) and Prem Ratan Dhan Payo (2015), and won the National Film Award for Best Direction for Uunchai (2022), the adventure drama starring Amitabh Bachchan, Anupam Kher and Boman Irani with Parineeti Chopra, made after a seven-year hiatus. His fourth film, Main Prem Ki Diwani Hoon (2003), starred Hrithik Roshan, Kareena Kapoor and Abhishek Bachchan.
notes: He is the grandson of Tarachand Barjatya, PERSON-233, written in batch 6, which makes this the roster's clearest three-generation link: the grandfather produced two Bachchan films in 1972–73, and the grandson directed one in 2022, both under the same banner, Rajshri Productions (PERSON-096). The National Film Award for Best Direction for Uunchai is stated as a win in the lead prose.

title: Sudhendu Roy
claims: Sudhendu Roy (1921–1999), born in Pabna in the Bengal Presidency and died in Mumbai, was an Indian film director, art director and production designer in Hindi cinema, active 1948–1999, best known for his realistic art direction in Bimal Roy's films such as Sujata (1959), Madhumati (1959) and Bandini (1963), and for glitzier work from Subhash Ghai's Karz (1980) and Karma (1986) to Yash Chopra's Silsila (1981), Chandni (1989) and Lamhe (1991). He won the Filmfare Award for Best Art Direction three times, for Madhumati (1959), Mere Mehboob (1964) and Sagina (1975). He also directed the Hindi films Uphaar (1971) and Saudagar (1973), both of which were India's official entry to the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. Uphaar was offered to him at the peak of his art-direction career by Tarachand Barjatya of Rajshri Productions; based on Rabindranath Tagore's story Samapti, it gave Jaya Bachchan her first solo lead. Saudagar followed, based on the Bengali story Ras by Narendranath Mitra and starring Nutan, Amitabh Bachchan and Padma Khanna; it was not a commercial success but received much critical acclaim and became India's Academy Award entry.
notes: One of very few people in this roster whose single Bachchan film was an official Indian Academy Award submission. He designed Silsila, a Bachchan film in this filmography, in his art-direction capacity — a function the collaborator roster does not track, so it is not counted. Tarachand Barjatya, who commissioned both of his directorial films, is PERSON-233.

title: Sultan Ahmed (director)
claims: Sultan Ahmed, born in Lucknow in the United Provinces and died in Tehran, Iran, on 22 May 2002, was an Indian film director, producer and writer of the 1970s and 1980s, known for his films about dacoits such as Heera, Ganga Ki Saugandh and Daata. He directed Rajesh Khanna and Jeetendra in Dharam Kanta, Amitabh Bachchan in Ganga Ki Saugandh, Sunil Dutt in Heera and Mithun Chakraborty in Daata, and the article records that he 'went on to sign Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha for Ganga Ki Saugand'. He received his first award for Heera from the Uttar Pradesh Film Journalist Association in 1973, a certificate of merit for Ganga Ki Saugandh from Tashkent in 1979, the K. Asif Memorial Award for 'Big Thinking' from the Bombay Film Awards Association for 1982–83, and the Punjabi Kala Sangam award for Daata, presented by President Giani Zail Singh. From 1990 to 1994 he served the Indian Motion Picture Producers' Association. His sons are Ali Akbar Sultan Ahmed and Ali Abbas Sultan Ahmed.
notes: The article's short description as fetched on this date reads 'Indian Hindu Phobic film director' — vandalism, not a description, and it is recorded here only so the discrepancy is on file; it is disregarded entirely and the body of the article, which is unaffected, is what this row rests on. No birth date is given anywhere in the article. This is the first instance of outright vandalism encountered in 306 collaborator articles, and it is a reminder that the short description, relied on throughout this project as the highest-yield verification signal, is itself an unprotected field.

title: Suneel Darshan
claims: Suneel Darshan is an Indian filmmaker, director, producer and writer working in the Hindi film industry. The article states that he was born into the Bhatt family, and records that his film starred Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar, Karisma Kapoor and Juhi Chawla.
notes: A poor article: it has no birth date, no filmography in the extract, a lead that opens mid-sentence with a stray image caption about a prayer meet for Sunil and Dharmesh Darshan's father, and an unexplained claim that he was 'born into Bhatt family' which nothing in the article supports. The claim is not repeated as fact here. His brother is the director Dharmesh Darshan. The film referred to is Ek Rishtaa: The Bond of Love (2001), the only credit counted.

title: T. J. Gnanavel
claims: T. J. Gnanavel is an Indian film director and screenwriter who works in the Tamil film industry. He was born in Chennai on 2 April and has been active since 2010. The article carries 'As film director' and 'As dialogue writer' filmography sections.
notes: A one-sentence lead with no year of birth and no named films in the extract; the substance of his row comes from the accompanying web search, SOURCE-887. He directed Vettaiyan (2024), Bachchan's Tamil-language debut.

title: Umesh Shukla
claims: Umesh Shukla is an Indian actor and director working in Hindi films, active since 1994, best known for the critically acclaimed comedy drama Oh My God. He made his directorial debut with Dhoondte Reh Jaaoge, presented by UTV Motion Pictures and Bindass. As an actor he is known for a villain role in Mithun Chakraborty's Yaar Gaddar, in which he played a governor. He has acted in and directed many Gujarati plays and is well known as the director of the Gujarati play Kanjee Viruddha Kanjee.
notes: The article has no birth date and its lead contains a garbled passage. Kanjee Viruddha Kanjee, the Gujarati play named here, is the source of Oh My God; the same Gujarati-theatre background produced 102 Not Out (2018), the film counted here, which is adapted from Saumya Joshi's Gujarati play and is the only credit in this filmography.

title: Vijay Anand (filmmaker)
claims: Vijay Anand (22 January 1934 – 23 February 2004), born in Gurdaspur, Punjab, and died in Mumbai, also known as Goldie Anand, was an Indian filmmaker, producer, screenwriter, editor and actor known for Guide (1965), Teesri Manzil (1966), Jewel Thief (1967) and Johny Mera Naam (1970). He made most of his films for the in-house banner Navketan Films and was part of the Anand family. He won the Filmfare Awards for Best Director and Best Dialogue for Guide (1965) and for Best Screenplay and Best Editing for Johny Mera Naam (1970), and BFJA awards as Best Editor for Johny Mera Naam (1970) and Double Cross (1972). As an actor his most memorable roles were in Kala Bazar (1960), Haqeeqat (1964), Kora Kagaz (1974), in which he starred opposite Jaya Bachchan, and Main Tulsi Tere Aangan Ki (1978).
notes: The infobox repeats the birth date in the death field, the known digest bug; dates are from the lead. The article does not mention Ram Balram (1980), the film counted here, which he directed, wrote and edited — the editing credit appears in that film's own infobox and matches his Filmfare-winning reputation as an editor. Raj Khosla's article (SOURCE-861) names him alongside Guru Dutt as a Hitchcock-influenced director.

title: Vijay Krishna Acharya
claims: Vijay Krishna Acharya is an Indian film director, screenwriter and dialogue writer known for his work in Hindi films and television shows. He was born in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, has been active since 2004, and is married to Anusheh Khan.
notes: A very thin article: no birth year, no named films in the extract, no awards and no mention of Bachchan. Thugs of Hindostan (2018), the film counted here, is one of the most expensive Hindi films ever made and one of its most prominent failures, and the article as cached says nothing about it.

title: Vikram Bhatt
claims: Vikram Bhatt is an Indian director, producer, screenwriter and actor, active since 1982, best known for directing the Raaz horror series produced by Mahesh and Mukesh Bhatt and for Ghulam (1998), starring Aamir Khan and Rani Mukherji and produced by Mukesh Bhatt; he was nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Director for both Ghulam (1999) and Raaz (2003). He belongs to the Bhatt film family: his father is the cinematographer Pravin Bhatt, his grandfather was Vijay Bhatt, his uncle is Arun Bhatt and his first cousin is the composer Chirantan Bhatt. He was formerly creative head of ASA Productions and Enterprises until he resigned in 2014, and many of his films were produced under Loneranger Productions, which he co-founded.
notes: Both entries in the awards table are nominations with blank Result cells, consistent with the lead, which describes them as nominations. The article has no birth date and does not mention Bachchan. His cousin Chirantan Bhatt is credited among the composers of Boss (FILM-217) in this filmography but has only that one credit and so is not in the roster.

title: Web search: Vishal Desai, credited co-director of Baghban
publisher: Web search (Filmibeat interview piece, 2007; Wikipedia articles on Baghban (2003 film) and Ravi Chopra; Letterboxd, TMDB, Indiancine.ma, Variety)
claims: Search summary: Vishal Desai served as an assistant director on Baghban (2003), which was directed by Ravi Chopra; he assisted Chopra on the film. A 2007 Filmibeat piece covers him as an actor — associated with Baghban, Baabul and the television show Banda Yeh Bindaas Hai — moving into direction. Every source located for Baghban itself, including Variety, Letterboxd, TMDB, Indiancine.ma and the Wikipedia article's own prose, names Ravi Chopra as the film's sole director.
notes: This substantiates the hypothesis recorded in batch 6 for Harish Razdan (SOURCE-840): Baghban's Wikipedia infobox lists four names in its director field — Ravi Chopra, Harish Razdan, Vishal Desai and Yatin Dang — and at least one of the three additional names is an *assistant* director, promoted into the infobox by an editor and copied into the Films sheet in phase 1. Separately, a 'Master Vishal Desai' appears in the Chupke Chupke (1975) cast as the child Bittoo; that is a different person and an unrelated name collision.

title: Web search: Vivek Shah, segment director of Darna Zaroori Hai
publisher: Web search (Moviebuff, TMDB, Letterboxd, IMDb full credits, Heroic Cinema; Wikipedia article on Darna Zaroori Hai)
claims: Search summary: Darna Zaroori Hai (2006), produced by Ram Gopal Varma and released on 28 April 2006, was directed by seven people, each taking a different part — J. D. Chakravarthy, Manish Gupta, Vivek Shah, Jijy Philip, Ram Gopal Varma, Sajid Khan and Prawaal Raman. The film interweaves six stories inside a frame narrative in which five children lost in a forest find a deserted house and an old woman who tells them six frightening tales. Vivek Shah directed one of the six segments.
notes: Wrong-article trap, caught by the short description and the mention counters. A bare Wikipedia fetch of 'Vivek Shah' resolves to 'Vivek R. Shah', a well-formed 5.8 KB article about an American businessman with zero occurrences of 'film' and zero of 'Bachchan'; it is not this person, and no article for the Indian director could be found. Which of the six stories he directed is not recorded by any source located. Bachchan appears only in the frame narrative, which Ram Gopal Varma directed, so this is a shared credit rather than a working relationship — the same situation as Jiji Philip (PERSON-262) and J. D. Chakravarthy (PERSON-261).

title: Vivek Sharma
claims: Vivek Sharma, born 27 August 1969 in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, is an Indian filmmaker and script-writer. The article states that he became recognised for his work when Amitabh Bachchan agreed to work with him on his directorial debut, Bhoothnath, and that in 2008 he turned independent filmmaker with Bhoothnath, described as 'one the biggest block buster', a very big cast film with Amitabh Bachchan, Juhi Chawla and Shah Rukh Khan.
notes: The article is short, ungrammatical and reads as promotional: its 'biggest blockbuster' characterisation of Bhoothnath is not supported by the film's own commercial record and is repeated here only as the article's claim, not as fact. Its one substantive point — that Bachchan's agreement to appear is what established Sharma's career — is plausible and consistent with the film being a first-time director's debut carried by a major star.

title: Web search: Yatin Dang, credited co-director of Baghban (negative result)
publisher: Web search (Wikipedia articles on Baghban (2003 film) and Ravi Chopra; Variety, Letterboxd, TMDB, Indiancine.ma, Cinemaazi, dbpedia)
claims: Search summary: no information about Yatin Dang was located. A search covering his name together with Baghban and its director credit returned nothing about him at all; every source found names Ravi Chopra as the film's director, with B. R. Chopra producing and co-writing for B. R. Films.
notes: The third and last of the disputed Baghban director credits, after Harish Razdan (PERSON-260, SOURCE-840) and Vishal Desai (PERSON-303, SOURCE-883), and the only one for whom nothing whatever could be established — no article, no credit, no birth date, no confirmation he worked on the film. Graded Unknown, like Harish Razdan. Since Vishal Desai is documented as an assistant director on the film, the likeliest reading is that all three additional infobox names are assistants.

title: Web search: T. J. Gnanavel, director of Jai Bhim and Vettaiyan
publisher: Web search (IMDb biography, Pinkvilla interview, IndiaGlitz, The Media Rumble, Rotten Tomatoes; Wikipedia articles on Jai Bhim (film) and Vettaiyan)
claims: Search summary: T. J. Gnanavel was born in Chennai, graduated from Loyola College, Chennai, holds a PhD in Tamil literature and worked as a journalist before entering cinema. He began as a dialogue writer on Raththa Sarithiram (2010) and Payanam (2011), then worked as an assistant director, and made his directorial debut in 2017 with the comedy Kootathil Oruthan, starring Ashok Selvan and Priya Anand, which drew average reviews. He received wide critical acclaim for Jai Bhim (2021), based on a case handled by Justice K. Chandru, whom Gnanavel had interviewed before Chandru took the case, while working for the magazine Ananda Vikatan. He then directed Vettaiyan (2024) starring Rajinikanth, and in the same year began work on Dosa King starring Mohanlal.
notes: Supplements the very thin Wikipedia article, SOURCE-878. Note the coincidence within this batch: Gnanavel worked as a journalist at Ananda Vikatan, the Tamil magazine that S. S. Balan (PERSON-289, SOURCE-869) edited for decades — two of the roster's 306 collaborators, separated by 52 years of filmmaking, connected through the same Chennai magazine.

title: Web search: Ribhu Dasgupta, Te3n and Yudh
publisher: Web search (IMDb, Letterboxd, BollySpice, News24; Wikipedia articles on Te3n and Ribhu Dasgupta)
claims: Search summary: Ribhu Dasgupta is an Indian film and television director who debuted with Michael (2011). Te3n (2016) is a Hindi action thriller written and directed by him, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Nawazuddin Siddiqui, Sabyasachi Chakraborty, Padmavati Rao and Vidya Balan, and is an official remake of the 2013 South Korean thriller Montage, reimagined as an investigation into child abductions. In 2013–14 he directed Yudh, a television mini-series for Sony Entertainment Television starring Amitabh Bachchan.
notes: Supplements the short Wikipedia article, SOURCE-866. The significant fact is the order of the two collaborations: Dasgupta directed Bachchan on television in Yudh in 2013–14, before directing him in Te3n in 2016, so the film was a continuation of an existing working relationship rather than a first meeting. Television is outside this workbook's scope, so Yudh appears in no sheet; it is recorded here as context. One search result was a Grokipedia page, which the workbook treats as unreliable and which is not relied on for any claim here.

title: Film Hi Film (1983)
claims: Synopsis: 'Pran struggles to make a film with newcomers but nobody is willing to finance his flick. Many big stars of 70/80's have special appearances.' Directed by Hiren Nag. The cast credits shown list only Pran Sikand, Ramesh Deo and Seema Deo; Amitabh Bachchan is not among them.
notes: Consulted on 18 September 2026 while resolving the scope question on this film. Used only for the frame story's premise and for the absence of Bachchan from the listed cast credits; the page says nothing about archive footage either way.

title: List of awards and nominations received by Amitabh Bachchan

notes: Downloaded as raw wikitext. Single-source for most award rows, so award rows carry Medium confidence; the page's own citations were not individually followed. The page's summary infobox reports 7 National Film Award nominations and 47 Filmfare nominations, but the page itemises only the 7 National wins and 34 Filmfare nominations; the unlisted nominations are not recorded here rather than being invented, so Awards under-counts those two ceremonies against the page's own totals.
